Fix UAF in command-socket --notify (#3988)

* Fix UAF in command-socket --notify

- Defer file-done notification to packet thread's FILE_DONE sentinel
  so the notification fires when packets have actually drained, not
  when the file has just been queued.
- Stop eagerly dereferencing the scheme actions slot while packets
  (and their sessions referencing actions->ops) are still in flight.
- Track load_thread recursion depth so the actions-held client ref
  is released exactly once at the outermost call, allowing the
  command-socket client to close after exit.

id API::Handlers::InfluxHandler::registerCommands()
{
  static auto& registry = CommandRegistry::instance();

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("influx.setConfig"),
    QStringLiteral("Configure the InfluxDB 2.x sink: server URL, organization, bucket and the "
                   "measurement every point is written under. Every field is optional, so a call "
                   "changes only what it names. The token is write-only: it goes to the "
                   "machine-bound credential vault, never to the project file, and no verb ever "
                   "reads it back."),
    API::makeSchema(
      {
  },
      {{QStringLiteral("url"),
        QStringLiteral("string"),
        QStringLiteral("Server URL, e.g. http://localhost:8086")},
       {QStringLiteral("org"),
        QStringLiteral("string"),
        QStringLiteral("Organization that owns the bucket")},
       {QStringLiteral("bucket"), QStringLiteral("string"), QStringLiteral("Destination bucket")},
       {QStringLiteral("measurement"),
        QStringLiteral("string"),
        QStringLiteral("Measurement name (default: serial_studio)")},
       {QStringLiteral("token"),
        QStringLiteral("string"),
        QStringLiteral("API token; stored in the credential vault, write-only")}}),
    &setConfig);

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("influx.setEnabled"),
    QStringLiteral("Enable or disable the InfluxDB sink for the current project. Requires a "
                   "valid commercial licence; an unlicensed build reports enabled=false."),
    API::makeSchema({
      {QStringLiteral("enabled"),
       QStringLiteral("boolean"),
       QStringLiteral("Whether to write points to InfluxDB")}
  }),
    &setEnabled);

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("influx.getStatus"),
    QStringLiteral("Snapshot the sink: enabled/isOpen, the endpoint fields, whether a token is "
                   "stored, and the pulled counters (pointsWritten, pointsDropped, "
                   "fieldsSkipped, httpErrors) plus the last write error."),
    API::emptySchema(),
    &getStatus);
}

::Drivers::Iec104::Iec104()
  : m_open(false)
  , m_loading(true)
  , m_started(false)
  , m_persistent(true)
  , m_clockValid(false)
  , m_port(Iec104Proto::kDefaultPort)
  , m_commonAddress(1)
  , m_windowK(kDefaultK)
  , m_windowW(kDefaultW)
  , m_timeoutT1(kDefaultT1Ms)
  , m_timeoutT2(kDefaultT2Ms)
  , m_timeoutT3(kDefaultT3Ms)
  , m_lastStampNs(0)
  , m_clockOffsetNs(0)
  , m_stationBaseMs(0)
  , m_linkDrops(0)
  , m_badQualityPoints(0)
  , m_skippedAsdus(0)
  , m_testTimeouts(0)
  , m_unstampedPoints(0)
  , m_framesPublished(0)
  , m_dirtyCount(0)
  , m_frameReserveBytes(OpcUaWire::kHeaderBytes)
  , m_host(QStringLiteral("127.0.0.1"))
  , m_timer(new QTimer(this))
  , m_socket(new QTcpSocket(this))
{
  loadSettings();
  applyProtocolParameters();
  m_loading = false;

  m_timer->setInterval(kIec104ProtocolTickMs);
  connect(m_timer, &QTimer::timeout, this, &IO::Drivers::Iec104::onProtocolTick);

  static constexpr void (Iec104::* kConfigSignals[])() = {&Iec104::hostChanged,
                                                          &Iec104::portChanged,
                                                          &Iec104::pointsChanged,
                                                          &Iec104::commonAddressChanged,
                                                          &Iec104::protocolParametersChanged};
  for (const auto signal : kConfigSignals)
    connect(this, signal, this, &IO::Drivers::Iec104::configurationChanged);

  Q_EMIT configurationChanged();
}

fluxDB::ExportWorker::ExportWorker(moodycamel::ReaderWriterQueue<DataModel::DataBlockPtr>* queue,
                                     std::atomic<bool>* enabled,
                                     std::atomic<size_t>* queueSize,
                                     std::atomic<quint64>* pointsWritten,
                                     std::atomic<quint64>* pointsDropped,
                                     std::atomic<quint64>* fieldsSkipped,
                                     std::atomic<quint64>* httpErrors)
  : DataModel::FrameConsumerWorker<DataModel::DataBlockPtr>(queue, enabled, queueSize)
  , m_manager(nullptr)
  , m_inFlightPoints(0)
  , m_epochOffsetNs(0)
  , m_healthy(false)
  , m_pointsWritten(pointsWritten)
  , m_pointsDropped(pointsDropped)
  , m_fieldsSkipped(fieldsSkipped)
  , m_httpErrors(httpErrors)
{
  SS_ASSERT_LOG(pointsWritten != nullptr);
  SS_ASSERT_LOG(pointsDropped != nullptr);
  SS_ASSERT_LOG(fieldsSkipped != nullptr);
  SS_ASSERT_LOG(httpErrors != nullptr);
}

fix(widgets): isolate the stereo eye channels and bound the 3D plot (spec 0072)

Spec 0071 moved the 3D plot onto the GPU and lost two properties the old
per-channel image merge gave for free.

Channel ownership was expressed as a colour: each ghost zeroed the
channels its eye did not own and drew as an ordinary blended stroke, so
it painted those channels black instead of leaving them alone -- the
light theme's minor grid went from pale cyan to muddy brown. Blending
the eyes over each other also attenuated whichever was drawn first,
worst at small eye separations where the ghosts almost coincide.
Ownership is now a render state instead: Plot3DEyeMaterial narrows
colorWrite in updateGraphicsPipelineState(), so the GPU never touches an
unowned channel and neither eye can dim the other. The alpha cap goes
with it -- it only existed to soften the blend. One node carries one
material, so grid, axis and trace accumulators become two-slot arrays,
slot 0 doubling as the whole mono picture. Pl

perf(console): gate the annotation decoder on a visible viewer

The decoder ran for every console chunk whether or not anything was on
screen to read the result, costing the stream a retained-window copy and
a decode() call per chunk with no consumer. AnnotationDecoder now tracks
views by identity through setViewerActive(); feed() returns before
ingestBytes() when the set is empty. The set is keyed by object because
two Terminal.qml instances can exist at once, and each entry carries a
destroyed() guard so a console window torn down with its panel open
cannot wedge the gate. Resuming clears the carry: those bytes predate
the gap, and splicing them onto what arrives after would hand decode() a
frame that was never on the wire.

Alongside it, three defects the gate work surfaced: exportCsv() reported
success on a device error because QTextStream's last buffered chunk
landed during destruction; trimToRetainedBytes() could strand an
out-of-order item behind a survivor once a backwards-anno

{
  return QStringLiteral(
    "decoder = {\n"
    "  rows: ['bytes', 'lines'],\n"
    "  classes: [{name: 'text', color: '#123456'}, 'newline'],\n"
    "  decode: function(bytes, offset, ctx) {\n"
    "    const b = new Uint8Array(bytes);\n"
    "    let i = 0;\n"
    "    while (i < b.length) {\n"
    "      const start = i;\n"
    "      while (i < b.length && b[i] !== 10) ++i;\n"
    "      if (i >= b.length) return start;\n"
    "      if (i > start) ctx.annotate(offset + start, offset + i - 1, 1, 0, ['line', 'L']);\n"

    "      ++i;\n"
    "    }\n"
    "    return i;\n"
    "  }\n"
    "};\n");

perf(widgets): render the 3D plot and the waterfall on the GPU (spec 0071)

Both widgets rebuilt full-screen CPU rasters on every display tick, and because
they rasterized on the GUI thread the cost landed on the same thread that
services the display tick and every other widget: one heavy widget degraded the
whole window. Plot3D allocated and cleared a screen-sized image per layer,
projected every point on the CPU and stroked the trace one antialiased segment
at a time; the waterfall smooth-scaled its entire history image per tick even
when a single row had changed.

Both are now QQuickItem scene-graph nodes. The trace and the grid become
coloured line strips, the waterfall history becomes a texture, and the text and
tick overlays move to their own translation units (Plot3D/Plot3DOverlay,
Waterfall/WaterfallOverlay). The stroke geometry builder that PlotCurve already
carried is extracted to Widgets::GpuStroke and shared by both, so there is one
scene-graph stroke path instead of two. A

feat(opcua): bound discovery and browse dials with deadlines

Discovery and the tag-picker browse had no upper bound: a server that
accepts the socket and then answers nothing never closes a channel, so
no session verdict was ever owed and the UI waited forever. Add
single-shot deadline timers for both, retire the session before
reporting so a late reply cannot report twice, and treat a bad-status
channel close under Intent::Discovering as the discovery verdict.

feat(opcua): secure channels, trust store and X.509 identity (spec 0067 stage 2)

Complete stage 2 of spec 0067 on top of the embedded open62541 + mbedTLS
stack: all five security policies, server-certificate verification against
a persistent trust store, and anonymous/username/X.509 identity tokens.

- OpcUaSecurity: client certificate identity, trust store, and the
  server-certificate verification callback feeding the trust decision.
- OpcUaSession: policy/mode negotiation, endpoint selection and identity
  token construction; discovery reports per-endpoint security.
- OpcUa driver: security configuration, failure verdicts distinguished
  from transport errors, and the trust prompt signal.
- OpcUaTrustDialog + setup-pane security group for the user-facing
  trust-on-first-use flow.
- OpcUaHandler: API commands for security configuration and trust
  decisions; EnumLabels gains the policy, mode and identity-token domains.
- Simulator serves secure endpoints and accepts X.509 identity,

feat(opcua): vendor open62541 + mbedTLS, add session facade (spec 0067 stage 1, partial)

Replaces the Qt6::OpcUa dependency with an OPC UA stack the repository owns. The Qt
plugin is absent from the commercial Qt build on Windows, and where present it resolves
its cryptography from a separately-shipped OpenSSL, so "missing" and "unloadable" gave
the same undiagnosable symptom and the driver was capped at security policy None.

Vendored under lib/:

- open62541 1.5.7, the published single-file distribution, already generated with
  UA_ENABLE_ENCRYPTION_MBEDTLS. One local patch (documented in lib/open62541/PATCHES.md):
  upstream generates the amalgamation on Linux and hardcodes UA_ARCHITECTURE_POSIX, which
  reaches <pthread.h> and fails on MSVC. Left undefined so upstream's own detection runs.
- Mbed TLS 3.6.7 (LTS), upstream source minus the test/program/doc trees. Not 4.x: the
  open62541 crypto plugin guards its API use with MBEDTLS_VERSION_NUMBER checks that stop
  at 3.x. Not the

plugin is absent from the commercial Qt build on Windows, and where present it resolves
its cryptography from a separately-shipped OpenSSL, so "missing" and "unloadable" gave
the same undiagnosable symptom and the driver was capped at security policy None.

Vendored under lib/:

- open62541 1.5.7, the published single-file distribution, already generated with
  UA_ENABLE_ENCRYPTION_MBEDTLS. One local patch (documented in lib/open62541/PATCHES.md):
  upstream generates the amalgamation on Linux and hardcodes UA_ARCHITECTURE_POSIX, which
  reaches <pthread.h> and fails on MSVC. Left undefined so upstream's own detection runs.
- Mbed TLS 3.6.7 (LTS), upstream source minus the test/program/doc trees. Not 4.x: the
  open62541 crypto plugin guards its API use with MBEDTLS_VERSION_NUMBER checks that stop
  at 3.x. Not the

Replaces the Qt6::OpcUa dependency with an OPC UA stack the repository owns. The Qt
plugin is absent from the commercial Qt build on Windows, and where present it resolves
its cryptography from a separately-shipped OpenSSL, so "missing" and "unloadable" gave
the same undiagnosable symptom and the driver was capped at security policy None.

Vendored under lib/:

- open62541 1.5.7, the published single-file distribution, already generated with
  UA_ENABLE_ENCRYPTION_MBEDTLS. One local patch (documented in lib/open62541/PATCHES.md):
  upstream generates the amalgamation on Linux and hardcodes UA_ARCHITECTURE_POSIX, which
  reaches <pthread.h> and fails on MSVC. Left undefined so upstream's own detection runs.
- Mbed TLS 3.6.7 (LTS), upstream source minus the test/program/doc trees. Not 4.x: the
  open62541 crypto plugin guards its API use with MBEDTLS_VERSION_NUMBER checks that stop
  at 3.x. Not the

plugin is absent from the commercial Qt build on Windows, and where present it resolves
its cryptography from a separately-shipped OpenSSL, so "missing" and "unloadable" gave
the same undiagnosable symptom and the driver was capped at security policy None.

Vendored under lib/:

- open62541 1.5.7, the published single-file distribution, already generated with
  UA_ENABLE_ENCRYPTION_MBEDTLS. One local patch (documented in lib/open62541/PATCHES.md):
  upstream generates the amalgamation on Linux and hardcodes UA_ARCHITECTURE_POSIX, which
  reaches <pthread.h> and fails on MSVC. Left undefined so upstream's own detection runs.
- Mbed TLS 3.6.7 (LTS), upstream source minus the test/program/doc trees. Not 4.x: the
  open62541 crypto plugin guards its API use with MBEDTLS_VERSION_NUMBER checks that stop
  at 3.x. Not the

static inline psa_key_type_t mbedtls_psa_translate_cipher_type(
    mbedtls_cipher_type_t cipher)
{
    switch (cipher) {
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_128_CCM:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_192_CCM:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_256_CCM:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_128_CCM_STAR_NO_TAG:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_192_CCM_STAR_NO_TAG:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_256_CCM_STAR_NO_TAG:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_128_GCM:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_192_GCM:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_256_GCM:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_128_CBC:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_192_CBC:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_256_CBC:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_128_ECB:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_192_ECB:
        case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_AES_256_ECB:
            return PSA_KEY_TYPE_AES;

        /* ARIA not yet supported in PSA. */
        /* case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_128_CCM:
           case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_192_CCM:
           case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_256_CCM:
           case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_128_CCM_STAR_NO_TAG:
           case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_192_CCM_STAR_NO_TAG:
           case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_256_CCM_STAR_NO_TAG:
           case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_128_GCM:
           case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_192_GCM:
           case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_256_GCM:
           case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_128_CBC:
           case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_192_CBC:
           case MBEDTLS_CIPHER_ARIA_256_CBC:
               return( PSA_KEY_TYPE_ARIA ); */

        default:
            return 0;
    }
}

::Drivers::OpcUa::OpcUa()
  : m_connecting(false)
  , m_discovering(false)
  , m_browsing(false)
  , m_pollMode(false)
  , m_persistent(true)
  , m_readInFlight(false)
  , m_subscribing(false)
  , m_hasDeferred(false)
  , m_pendingDial(PendingDial::None)
  , m_clockValid(false)
  , m_authMode(0)
  , m_endpointIndex(-1)
  , m_publishingInterval(kDefaultIntervalMs)
  , m_pendingMonitors(0)
  , m_failedMonitors(0)
  , m_revisedInterval(0)
  , m_frameCursor(0)
  , m_readLimit(kDefaultReadLimit)
  , m_valuesReceived(0)
  , m_badStatusCount(0)
  , m_unstampedCount(0)
  , m_framesPublished(0)
  , m_linkDrops(0)
  , m_skippedPolls(0)
  , m_endpointUrl(QStringLiteral("opc.tcp://127.0.0.1:4840"))
  , m_dialTimer(new QTimer(this))
  , m_watchdog(new QTimer(this))
  , m_pollTimer(new QTimer(this))
  , m_frameTimer(new QTimer(this))
  , m_client(nullptr)
  , m_browseClient(nullptr)
  , m_discoveryClient(nullptr)
  , m_tagModel(nullptr)
  , m_frameBytes(0)
  , m_lastStampNs(0)
  , m_lastNotifyNs(0)
  , m_serverOffsetMs(0)
  , m_clockOffsetNs(0)
  , m_vault(QStringLiteral("opcua"))
{
  loadSettings();

  m_dialTimer->setSingleShot(true);
  connect(m_dialTimer, &QTimer::timeout, this, &IO::Drivers::OpcUa::onDialTimeout);
  connect(m_pollTimer, &QTimer::timeout, this, &IO::Drivers::OpcUa::onPollTick);
  connect(m_frameTimer, &QTimer::timeout, this, &IO::Drivers::OpcUa::onFrameTick);
  connect(m_watchdog, &QTimer::timeout, this, &IO::Drivers::OpcUa::onWatchdogTick);

  static constexpr void (OpcUa::* kConfigSignals[])() = {&OpcUa::endpointUrlChanged,
                                                         &OpcUa::endpointIndexChanged,
                                                         &OpcUa::endpointsChanged,
                                                         &OpcUa::authModeChanged,
                                                         &OpcUa::usernameChanged,
                                                         &OpcUa::passwordChanged,
                                                         &OpcUa::publishingIntervalChanged,
                                                         &OpcUa::tagsChanged};
  for (const auto signal : kConfigSignals)
    connect(this, signal, this, &IO::Drivers::OpcUa::configurationChanged);

  QLoggingCategory::setFilterRules(QStringLiteral("*font*=false\n"
                                                  "qt.canbus*=false\n"
                                                  "qt.opcua*=false"));

  Q_EMIT configurationChanged();
}

::Drivers::OpcUaWire::Type IO::Drivers::OpcUaTagModel::wireTypeFromDataTypeId(
  const QString& dataTypeId) noexcept
{
  using OpcUaWire::Type;
  static const QHash<int, Type> k_map = {
    {  1, Type::Bool},
    {  2,   Type::I8},
    {  3,   Type::U8},
    {  4,  Type::I16},
    {  5,  Type::U16},
    {  6,  Type::I32},
    {  7,  Type::U32},
    {  8,  Type::I64},
    {  9,  Type::U64},
    { 10,  Type::F32},
    { 11,  Type::F64},
    { 12,  Type::Str},
    { 13,  Type::Str},
    { 14,  Type::Str},
    { 15,  Type::Str},
    { 16,  Type::Str},
    { 17,  Type::Str},
    { 18,  Type::Str},
    { 19,  Type::U32},
    { 20,  Type::Str},
    { 21,  Type::Str},
    { 26,  Type::F64},
    { 27,  Type::I64},
    { 28,  Type::U64},
    { 29,  Type::I32},
    {288,  Type::U32},
    {289,  Type::U64},
    {290,  Type::F64},
    {291,  Type::Str},
    {292,  Type::Str},
    {293,  Type::Str},
    {294,  Type::Str},
  };

  if (!dataTypeId.startsWith(QLatin1String("ns=0;i=")))
    return Type::Invalid;

  bool ok         = false;
  const int ident = dataTypeId.mid(7).toInt(&ok);
  if (!ok)
    return Type::Invalid;

  return k_map.value(ident, Type::Invalid);
}

  replay resends structure after a dashboard reset; notify gate avoids the
  reconfigure loop

  re-queue while injecting

  and batch rows to kFrameBlockSampleCap with the sink mask on
  DataBlock::masked so tick-flushed blocks never leak into recordings
- Release replay pool storage and shrink player buffers when the last
  player closes; remove all [SS0064] instrumentation

feat(dataflow): unify frame publication on a pooled block lane (specs 0054-0062)

Replaces the per-frame TimestampedFrame publication with a single pooled
DataModel::DataBlock lane: FrameBuilder stages parsed rows and flushes on the
display tick or a sample cap, structure travels separately as a
StructureSnapshot on pool-generation bumps, and stream workers emit blockReady
queued to the pipeline thread so every sink keeps a single producer. Sinks
share one clone_block_trimmed copy, since a queued sink holding a pool slot
would starve staging and drop frames from the exports too.

Landed together because they share that lane and would not build apart:

- 0054 session recording for stream-lane sources (columnar block codec,
  legacy v1/v2 database fixtures, sparse CSV row merger)
- 0055 unified block publication lane (DataBlock, two sample caps, snapshot
  structure, rate-sized time rings)
- 0056 connect-path crashes surfaced by the integration sweep (nested
  QEventLoop in connectDevice

         "  samples         BLOB NOT NULL"

DataModel::DataBlock lane: FrameBuilder stages parsed rows and flushes on the
display tick or a sample cap, structure travels separately as a
StructureSnapshot on pool-generation bumps, and stream workers emit blockReady
queued to the pipeline thread so every sink keeps a single producer. Sinks
share one clone_block_trimmed copy, since a queued sink holding a pool slot
would starve staging and drop frames from the exports too.

  structure, rate-sized time rings)

perf(memory): bound the frame pool by bytes and stop paying for idle stream exports

Large projects made the 8192-slot frame pool a memory sink: every publish could walk
to a virgin slot and fault in a permanent full-frame copy the pool never released.
Slot selection moves into DataModel::FramePoolPolicy (own TU, pure bookkeeping) and
gains a memory ceiling derived from the current frame's footprint, re-derived on
structural change only.

The dashboard-only republish now uses acquireReusedFrame(): it claims the source's
own slot or gives up. A refresh carries no new data, so skipping it is free, while
walking to a fresh slot would materialise another full copy. Export republishes keep
the normal acquire, so a recorded frame is never dropped for slot pressure.

fix: close the v4.0.3..HEAD release review (blockers, security, deps)

Findings from a review of the whole v4.0.3..HEAD range. Every claim below was
re-checked against the source; nothing here has been verified at runtime.

Thread teardown (ship blockers). Spec 0051 moved the frame pipeline onto its
own thread but teardown did not follow. StreamWorker::stop() and
PipelineHost::shutdown() guarded only on isRunning(), which a hung Fast-mode
script never satisfies, so the explicit call and the destructor's repeat call
each paid the full 5 s join timeout and then destroyed the QThread while its
OS thread was still executing Lua. StreamWorker's QThread was a value member
with no way to keep it alive; it is now a releasable unique_ptr like
PipelineHost's. The abandon latch carries idempotency and releases the thread
on the timeout path, and SessionContext::shutdown() also leaks the pipeline
host when abandoned, since the thread's frame router and reader wirings
capture it. The four replay en

perf(ui): gate hidden widgets and stop per-tick QML list churn

Every dashboard widget wired to Dashboard::updated now skips its refresh
while effectively invisible (any inactive workspace page) and pulls a
fresh snapshot via itemChange(ItemVisibleHasChanged) on the next show,
so a 100-widget project only pays for the active page.

BarPanel drops its seven NOTIFY-updated list properties for one int
revision counter plus scalar Q_INVOKABLE accessors: a tick now converts
a handful of scalars to JS instead of every per-row QVector/QStringList
per binding. The extremes markers in BarPanel, Bar, Gauge and Meter QML
switch from a rebuilt-per-tick JS array model to a fixed two-delegate
model that toggles visibility, ending per-tick delegate churn.

DataGrid caches each row's raw value and formats only on change, so
static rows never allocate; ExtensionData is deliberately left ungated
(spec 0038 extensions may process data while hidden).

feat(scripting): replace the vendored Lua 5.4 runtime with LuaJIT (spec 0051 M2)

LuaJIT 2.1 (pinned 1edc3e52b67) now backs every Lua surface, built by a
CMake port of its two-stage DynASM/buildvm flow. The user surface is
Lua 5.1 + shims: LUA52COMPAT, a bit32 table over the native bit library,
and LuaCompatJIT.h restoring the newer C-API subset under canonical
names. Every VM setup path runs under a protected bootstrap so the panic
handler is unreachable, and all Lua includes gained extern "C" (the old
tree was compiled as C++).

A per-project Safe/Fast mode ships with it: Safe (default) runs the
interpreter with the count-hook watchdog; Fast enables the JIT and
trades the watchdog away behind a native consent box (hooks never fire
inside compiled traces, so it is one switch, not two). Macros and the
MQTT publisher stay pinned Safe.

The shipped script corpus (10 parsers, 2 transforms) and both importer
generators were migrated off 5.3 bitwise syntax; the Modbus generator's
string.unp

LuaJIT 2.1 (pinned 1edc3e52b67) now backs every Lua surface, built by a
CMake port of its two-stage DynASM/buildvm flow. The user surface is
Lua 5.1 + shims: LUA52COMPAT, a bit32 table over the native bit library,
and LuaCompatJIT.h restoring the newer C-API subset under canonical
names. Every VM setup path runs under a protected bootstrap so the panic
handler is unreachable, and all Lua includes gained extern "C" (the old
tree was compiled as C++).

A per-project Safe/Fast mode ships with it: Safe (default) runs the
interpreter with the count-hook watchdog; Fast enables the JIT and
trades the watchdog away behind a native consent box (hooks never fire
inside compiled traces, so it is one switch, not two). Macros and the
MQTT publisher stay pinned Safe.

The shipped script corpus (10 parsers, 2 transforms) and both importer
generators were migrated off 5.3 bitwise syntax; the Modbus generator's
string.unp

feat(datamodel): replace the global parse breaker with a fair-share governor (spec 0051 M1)

The fixed-window breaker starved every source when one source's scripts
went over budget (BADAQ: CAN frozen to 1 Hz by two audio sources). The
new ParseBudget engine charges parse time per source into EWMA duty
estimates (offered-load scaled, 0.90/0.70 hysteresis), decimates only
sources above their fair share, recovers continuously, and is swept from
the 1 Hz tick so a silenced offender can never latch stale state. The
overload is now self-diagnosing: a per-source problem-center finding and
a taskbar badge replace the old one-shot message box.

Spec 0051 artifacts (spec/plan/tasks), ctest suite (6 cases), pytest
integration suite (3 tests, validated against the rebuilt binary), and
the qt-cpp-review findings log ride along. Singleton census re-baselined
(+3 sites, checker free functions + Dashboard poll).

feat(sessions): verify archived session reproducibility (spec 0044)

An archived session already carries the raw device bytes, the recorded values and the
project JSON that interpreted them, but nothing ever replayed one against the other, so
reproducibility was a claim rather than a checked invariant. A verification pass now
re-records the archived bytes with the archived project on the current build and diffs the
result against what was captured.

Capture side: ExportWorker keeps incremental SHA-256 fingerprints over the raw chunks and
the readings rows (canonical layout in Sessions::hashRawChunk / hashReadingRow, shared with
the verifier so the byte layout has one definition), and finalizeSession stamps them into
the session row with app_version, capture_format, repro_class and the sampled link-loss
counters.

Verify side: Sessions::Verifier drives a child process (--verify-session, --verify-session-id,
--verify-keep-regen) so a replay can never disturb the live session; the child w

refactor: drop the async connection-flow layer from the IO drivers

Connection orchestration goes back to the synchronous open() path each
driver already implemented. IO::ConnectionFlows and the HAL_Driver async
hooks (supportsAsyncOpen/beginOpen/abortOpen/openTimeoutMsec, the
openFinished and linkDropped signals) are gone, along with the per-device
TaskRunner in DeviceManager and the task trees in BluetoothLE, MQTT,
Modbus and Network. ConnectionManager keeps activeFlowCount,
reconnectAttempt and hasPendingOpen as constant stubs so the QML and API
surfaces stay intact.

app/src/Async (TaskTree, RetryPolicy, AsyncClock) stays: MQTT::Publisher
and the connection diagnostics still use it, and its two ctest suites
still run. The suites that covered the removed layer
(tst_connection_flows, tst_hal_driver) are dropped.

Also restores the GPL-3.0-or-later SPDX headers on the nine IO files that
came back with the pre-relicense header, refreshes the translations and
normalizes the bundled exam

feat: MQTT mutual TLS with client certificates (spec 0041)

Both MQTT surfaces (the subscriber data source and the publisher) can now present an X.509
client certificate and its private key during the TLS handshake, which is what AWS IoT
Core, Azure IoT Hub, and PKI-fronted corporate brokers require. Adds an optional ALPN
protocol field (defaulting to AWS IoT's x-amzn-mqtt-ca) so the 443 endpoint works too.

MQTT::TlsIdentity is the shared loader: it reads PEM/DER certificates and keys, detects the
key algorithm, applies the passphrase, and reports why a pair was rejected instead of
failing the handshake with no explanation. The passphrase goes through CredentialVault; the
project file stores only paths.

fix: build licensing first and revalidate rejected cached licenses (spec 0042)

A machine whose cached license restore was rejected at startup (grace expired, machine-id
drift, decrypt failure) stayed unlicensed for the whole session: the restore clears the
in-memory licensing data, and the startup online validation was gated on that same data
being present, so the one case that needs a live server verdict never asked for one. Adds
LemonSqueezy::revalidateCachedLicense() for that path and liveVerdict() to keep cached and
live responses from being confused.

The licensing block (MachineID, LemonSqueezy, OfflineLicense, Trial) now constructs right
after Translator instead of after AppState, so the CommercialToken is final-for-startup
before any entitlement consumer constructs or restores state; the ctor-edge proof for the
new order is checked in under spec 0001. Consumer inventory lives in the spec folder.

fix: free the adjusted argv only after ~QApplication runs

QApplication reads argv for its whole lifetime (origArgv string compares on
Windows), but main() freed the heap-duplicated array before the application
object died -- a use-after-free read in the exact region the Windows CI run
now reaches since the FrameConsumer join fix (0xC0000005 after teardown).
The application lifecycle moves into runApplication() so main() releases
argv after ~QApplication, and the release now frees a pointer snapshot
taken at adjustment time: Qt compacts recognized arguments in place, so
freeing by the live array and count double-frees shifted entries and leaks
removed ones. Early CLI exits now release the array too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: join FrameConsumer workers before SessionContext::shutdown()

Spec 0039 moved the core modules' destruction into main(), ahead of the
static destruction that joins exporter worker threads; a worker ticking in
that window writes into freed module memory (QString refcount on
ProjectModel::title(), freed device map in isConnected()), which Windows
reports as heap corruption 0xC0000374 in the big_db_test CI run. onQuit()
now stops every FrameConsumer worker while qApp is alive and drains the
previously unlisted Console::Export backlog. Census re-baselined: the sweep
reaches Meyers-singleton exporters from the composition root's teardown
owner, where no SessionContext injection path exists.

void API::Handlers::DiagnosticsHandler::registerCommands()
{
  static auto& registry = CommandRegistry::instance();

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("diagnostics.run"),
    QStringLiteral("Check whether this machine is set up to connect: serial-port permissions "
                   "and the exact command that fixes them on Linux, Bluetooth adapter power and "
                   "permission, audio inputs, and whether the configured host or broker "
                   "resolves and accepts a connection. THE first call when a connection fails "
                   "or the Connect button does nothing. Returns immediately with the instant "
                   "results already complete; slower reachability probes finish in the "
                   "background. Optional param: bus."),
    makeSchema(
      {
  },
      {{QStringLiteral("bus"),
        QStringLiteral("string"),
        QStringLiteral("Only check this bus: serial, bluetooth, network, broker or audio. "
                       "Omitted means every bus this build supports.")}}),
    &run);

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("diagnostics.status"),
    QStringLiteral("Report whether a diagnostics run is still probing, when the last run "
                   "finished, and how many results of each verdict stand. Poll this after "
                   "diagnostics.run, then read the findings with problems.list filtered by "
                   "checkerId 'diagnostics.<bus>'."),
    emptySchema(),
    &status);
}

                   "flag, and the serialized project. Large projects are delivered as base64 "
                   "parts; read structureParts from mirror.getInfo and pass part."),
    makeSchema(

        QStringLiteral("integer"),

void API::Handlers::ProblemsHandler::registerCommands()
{
  static auto& registry = CommandRegistry::instance();
  const auto empty      = emptySchema();

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("problems.list"),
    QStringLiteral("List the diagnostics Serial Studio currently reports about the loaded "
                   "project, the live link and the parser/transform scripts. THE first call "
                   "when a dashboard is blank, a widget stays empty or values look wrong: each "
                   "finding names the concrete cause, a remedy and the entity to fix. Optional "
                   "params: severity (info/warning/error), checkerId, limit."),
    makeSchema(
      {
  },
      {{QStringLiteral("severity"),
        QStringLiteral("string"),
        QStringLiteral("Only findings at this severity: info, warning or error.")},
       {QStringLiteral("checkerId"),
        QStringLiteral("string"),
        QStringLiteral("Only findings produced by this checker; see problems.listCheckers.")},
       {QStringLiteral("limit"),
        QStringLiteral("integer"),
        QStringLiteral("Max findings to return (default 50, max 200).")}}),
    &list);

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("problems.run"),
    QStringLiteral("Re-run every registered diagnostic checker and return the refreshed list "
                   "in the same shape as problems.list. Read-only: checkers inspect the "
                   "project, the link counters and the script engines, and never modify them. "
                   "Use it after an edit to confirm a finding actually cleared."),
    empty,
    &run);

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("problems.listCheckers"),
    QStringLiteral("List the registered diagnostic checkers and the triggers each one answers "
                   "to (projectChanged, linkSample, onDemand), so you can see what "
                   "problems.run covers and filter problems.list by checkerId."),
    empty,
    &listCheckers);
}

static void inspectDatasetReferences(const DataModel::Dataset& dataset,
                                     const QSet<int>& datasetIds,
                                     QList<Finding>& out)
{
  if (dataset.xAxisId > 0 && !datasetIds.contains(dataset.xAxisId))
    out.append(makeFinding(Misc::ProblemCenter::Error,
                           "dangling-x-axis",
                           trProblem("Plot X-axis points at a deleted dataset"),
                           trProblem("\"%1\" plots against dataset %2, which is not part of this "
                                     "project any more.")
                             .arg(datasetLabel(dataset))
                             .arg(dataset.xAxisId),
                           trProblem("Pick an existing dataset as the X-axis, or switch the axis "
                                     "back to Time or Samples."),
                           dataset.uniqueId,
                           kJumpDataset));

  if (dataset.waterfallYAxis > 0 && !datasetIds.contains(dataset.waterfallYAxis))
    out.append(makeFinding(Misc::ProblemCenter::Error,
                           "dangling-waterfall-axis",
                           trProblem("Waterfall Y-axis points at a deleted dataset"),
                           trProblem("\"%1\" reads its waterfall Y-axis from dataset %2, which is "
                                     "not part of this project any more.")
                             .arg(datasetLabel(dataset))
                             .arg(dataset.waterfallYAxis),
                           trProblem("Pick an existing dataset as the Y-axis, or switch it back "
                                     "to Time."),
                           dataset.uniqueId,
                           kJumpDataset));
}

static void checkPlotRange(const DataModel::Dataset& dataset, QList<Finding>& out)
{
  if (!dataset.plt || !rangeIsBroken(dataset.pltMin, dataset.pltMax))
    return;

  out.append(makeFinding(Misc::ProblemCenter::Warning,
                         "inverted-plot-range",
                         trProblem("Plot range is inverted or empty"),
                         trProblem("\"%1\" has a plot minimum of %2 and a maximum of %3, so the "
                                   "curve has no room to be drawn.")
                           .arg(datasetLabel(dataset))
                           .arg(dataset.pltMin)
                           .arg(dataset.pltMax),
                         trProblem("Set the plot maximum above the plot minimum, or set both to "
                                   "zero to scale the axis automatically."),
                         dataset.uniqueId,
                         kJumpDataset));
}

static void reportDisabledEngine(const DataModel::ScriptStat& stat, QList<Finding>& out)
{
  out.append(makeFinding(Misc::ProblemCenter::Error,
                         "parser-disabled",
                         trProblem("Frame parser was switched off"),
                         trProblem("The frame parser of \"%1\" exceeded its time budget on too "
                                   "many consecutive frames and was switched off. Last error: %2")
                           .arg(sourceLabel(stat.sourceId), stat.lastError),
                         trProblem("Simplify the parser so it returns within the frame budget, "
                                   "then reload the script to re-enable it."),
                         -1,
                         QString()));
}

fix(licensing): keep a running trial on the full Pro feature set

The rocket demo's Mission View painter never rendered under a trial. The cause
was not a tier gate -- no trial-excluding gate for the painter exists -- but a
one-shot mutation: DemoLauncher::applyProGating() baked proWidgetsEnabled()
into the group's enabled flag at demo-start, and the bundled project shipped
that group disabled. A capability token that landed after that instant left the
group switched off, recoverable only if activatedChanged fired while the demo
was already the open project.

Ship every demo group enabled and delete applyProGating() with its license
hook. Dashboard::buildWidgetGroups already resolves Pro state per reconfigure
and holds the painter fallback, so the license no longer has to win a race.

translate: read flag emoji instead of spelling them out (#2463)

A lone flag emoji was read correctly, but any flag with something next to
it was not. Four separate defects were behind this.

Adjacent emoji were merged into a single token. Single-codepoint emoji
survived that by accident, because the letter-by-letter spelling fallback
looks up each codepoint and finds it in the emoji dictionary. A flag is
two regional indicators, so a run of flags matched nothing and was read
as "symbol 1F1F0, symbol 1F1FF, ...". Break the token between adjacent
emoji, keeping skin tone modifiers attached to their base and joining
regional indicators in pairs.

Tag characters (U+E0020..U+E007F) were dropped before the dictionary
lookup, so the subdivision flags of England, Scotland and Wales were read
as "black flag" even though their entries exist. Keep them in the word,
and fall back to the base emoji name for a subdivision with no entry of
its own, so an unlisted one does not fall silent.

tolower()

replaces that with ffc, a pure-C99 single-header correctly-rounded float parser

[Keyboard Manager] Fix stuck modifiers and dropped key-to-text remaps (#48571)

## Summary
Fixes stuck modifier keys and silently-dropped remaps on Keyboard
Manager's **single key → text** path, and adds unit coverage (including
a mockable injection-failure seam).

## What this changes
1. **Insert a dummy key event before releasing held modifiers.**
Releasing a lone Win or Alt key-up otherwise triggers the Start Menu /
menu bar. The dummy key absorbs it so the release is inert. The dummy +
releases are only injected when a modifier is actually held.
2. **Accept `WM_SYSKEYDOWN` as well as `WM_KEYDOWN`.** While Alt is held
the system delivers `WM_SYSKEYDOWN`, so the previous `WM_KEYDOWN`-only
guard silently dropped the remap whenever Alt was down.
3. **Route `Helpers::SendTextInput` through `InputInterface`** instead
of calling Win32 `SendInput` directly. Besides making the path mockable,
this stops the existing unit tests from injecting real keystrokes into
the OS during a test run. Tex

[KeyboardManager] Fix sticky Ctrl caused by stale AltGr flag (#46672)

## Summary

Fixes #46693

- The `static bool isAltRightKeyInvoked` flag in
`HandleShortcutRemapEvent` is set when AltGr (RAlt+LCtrl) is pressed,
but only reset inside Case 1's else branch — which requires a shortcut
to be actively invoked (`isShortcutInvoked == true`)
- If the user presses and releases AltGr when **no shortcut is active**,
the flag stays `true` permanently across all future calls
- Once stale, the flag blocks modifier key restoration and state resets
at 13 locations throughout the function (lines 646, 670, 791, 800, 866,
880, 889, 907, 927, 978, 996), and causes LCtrl key-up events to `break`
out of the handler loop (line 620-622) instead of being properly
processed
- This makes LCtrl permanently stuck for any shortcut remap that uses
LCtrl as a modifier

## Fix

Reset `isAltRightKeyInvoked` when `VK_RMENU` (Right Alt) is released,
regardless of whether a shortcut is currently invoked. This is added

CPU: KV cache quantization — KV8 (fp8 e4m3) + KV_TQ (rotated-int4 / PolarQuant)

Latent-KV cache quantization for the MLA attention, CPU path only — the CUDA
and Metal kernels are follow-up PRs, each gated by a hardware owner.

- KV8=1: fp8 e4m3 byte cache + per-row f32 scale (~3.9x less KV RAM). The CPU
  consumer LUT-decodes inline in the score/context dot products; the per-row
  scale factors out of the sums.
- KV_TQ=4: rotated-int4 codec (randomized-Hadamard rotation + Lloyd codebook,
  radius rides the per-row scale). The consumer uses the rotation's
  orthogonality (q.x_hat == rotate(q).c): rotate the query once per head, dot
  the packed nibbles through the 16-level codebook, unrotate the accumulated
  context once — the cache is never reconstructed. KV_TQ=2|3|5|6 and
  KV_TQ_POLAR=1 use the PolarQuant codec (recursive-polar, variable bits).
- .coli_kv persistence: v2 (KV8) / v3 (KV_TQ) formats; the file magic encodes
  the tier and h[7] the TQ codec+bits. Any mode mismatch is r

Separate a formal's ABI position from its sdb index ##analysis

arg_index counts placed arguments and must stay dense, because
apply_debug_info stops reading at the first missing fcn.%s.arg.%d key.
It was also passed as the formal's ABI position, so the two diverged the
moment a formal was skipped, and every later fallback was handed its
neighbour's register. Count non-result formals separately and pass that
as argno; argc now counts non-result formals too, which is what feeds
the stack-offset math for reverse conventions.

The calling convention tables describe integer slots only, so a float
formal without a location was placed in an integer register it never
occupies, colliding with a located argument sitting there. Skip the
fallback for floating-point and complex types instead.

On bins/elf/dwarf_go_tree that removes four float64 and three complex128
arguments from integer registers, and without the argno fix the removal
shifts twelve later arguments down a slot.

Read DW_AT_variabl

Zero-extend 32-bit register writes on arm64 ##esil

A write to a `w` register clears the top half of the `x` register it sits
in. ESIL does not do that on its own: naming `w9` stores four bytes and
leaves the rest of `x9` as it was, so

    ar x9=0xffffffff00000001
    ar x10=1
    wx 29010a0b       ; add w9, w9, w10
    aes; ar x9
    before  0xffffffff00000002
    after   0x2

The same held for every `w` destination: the arithmetic helpers, the
loads, the moves. It is appended once where the instruction's ESIL is
finished rather than at each of the sites that spell a destination, and
after the flag assignments so the extension cannot disturb the comparison
state they read. Storing through the 64-bit name clears the top half
without reading it, so `aea` still reports only what is really read.

Five expectations move, all because a 32-bit write now fully defines its
register and the type backtrace can follow it:

- db/anal/types: `mov w0, 1` picks up `int fd`
- db/anal/jmptbl: the thre

LFRFID Wipe T5577: progress bar + review/simplify fixes

Replace the static "Wiping" popup with a progress bar that fills over the
read-back verify window. A periodic timer drives both the bar and the verify
deadline (rename LfRfidEventWipeVerifyTimeout -> LfRfidEventWipeProgress).

Fixes from the review/simplify pass:
- Widen the verify window 4500 -> 6000 ms. A full Auto ASK+PSK no-decode
  cycle is ~5 s (450 ms stabilize + 2000 ms switch per feature, x2 + drops),
  so 4500 ms could expire mid-PSK and falsely report "Wiped!" on a non-wiped
  PSK tag. The old rationale comment was wrong; corrected to match.
- Add a _Static_assert that the verify window is an integer multiple of the
  tick period, so the bar and the success deadline cannot silently drift.

  failure teardown paths cannot drift apart.

LFRFID: add Wipe T5577 to Extra Actions

Adds a Proxmark3-style "lf t55xx wipe" to the Extra Actions menu, under
"Clear T5577 Password". Writes the factory default config (0x000880E0:
ASK/Manchester, RF/32, 7 data blocks, no password) to block 0 and zeros
all other page-0 blocks, leaving the tag in a blank, openly re-writable
state.

Unlike Clear T5577 Password (which only resets block 0 + the password and
leaves the tag readable), Wipe destroys the stored data, so the result is
verified by reading back: after the write the worker does a read-any pass
and, if nothing decodes within the window, reports success; if the tag
still decodes, the wipe did not take (e.g. password-protected) and it
reports failure.

v1 does a no-password wipe: works on unprotected tags; protected tags are
reported as "Not Wiped". UI is monochrome-friendly (no red/green):
neutral cyan activity blink, distinct icons + single/double vibro for the
result, and a single Back press returns to the menu.

New scenes: wi

Adds a Proxmark3-style "lf t55xx wipe" to the Extra Actions menu, under
"Clear T5577 Password". Writes the factory default config (0x000880E0:
ASK/Manchester, RF/32, 7 data blocks, no password) to block 0 and zeros

Hardware test (per-block select) cloned the tag, but the 8265 only began
TTF emission a power cycle later, so its own read-back verify missed it and

  protocol, e.g. [EM4100] / (T5577) / (EM4305) / (8265/H5), so the multi-
  attempt sweep is visible instead of lo

LFRFID Hitag micro: send full select chain before write (open-loop)

A Proxmark3 `lf hitag htu` clone trace shows the 8265 only honors a WRITE
after a closed-loop select: READ UID -> GET SYSTEM INFO -> READ config ->
LOGIN, with the tag responding to each. Our previous blind LOGIN+WRITE
skipped all of that, so the chip was never selected and ignored us
(writes did nothing on 8265/8210/H5.5).

Send the whole chain open-loop: transmit READ UID, SYSINFO, READ config,
LOGIN, then the three WRITEs, waiting out each (unread) tag response
window between commands (waits derived from the PM3 trace). The tag still
selects/authenticates on receipt; we just can't observe it (no RX).

Frame builders for READ UID / SYSINFO / READ MULTIPLE BLOCK were added and
verified byte-identical to the PM3 trace (e.g. READ UID 22 04 ..,
READ 22 5F ..). Restructured so each frame's bit-banging is its own short
FURI_CRITICAL section and the long inter-frame waits run with interrupts
enabled.

SubGhz: add Telcoma/Cardin EDGE protocol

Static (fixed-code) 433.92 MHz OOK/AM Manchester remote from the Telcoma /
Cardin EDGE family (EDGE2 / EDGE4 / EDGE20; sold compatible with TANGO /
QUASAR / SLIM / SE). Frame = 0xFF preamble + per-remote serial + a one-hot
channel marker; decoded to a canonical 32-bit key where key[31:24]=0xFF,
key[23:3]=serial, key[2:0]=one-hot channel (gate=0, others 1/2/4). The
channel-aware encoder reproduces each channel's exact waveform (gate channel
verified against the original remote's RF; gate frame is 32 data bits + a
required HIGH stop half-bit, other channels are 33 bits with no stop).

This is the EDGE 433.92 fixed-code protocol; it is NOT the existing Cardin
S449 (FSK KeeLoq rolling) or S466 (27 MHz PWM), which are different products.

- decoder + encoder: lib/subghz/protocols/telcoma_edge.{c,h}
- registered in protocol_items.{c,h}
- unit tests + sample captures covering the 32-bit (gate) and 33-bit
  (channel) decode paths
- listed in documentat

streaming: serve mixed-precision routed experts (per-layer boosted quants)

GGUFs whose routed experts are not uniformly quantized across layers (e.g.
IQ2_XXS/Q2_K everywhere with a few layers upcast to Q4_K via --tensor-type)
failed every request under --ssd-streaming: the batch-selected-addr prefill
maps layers with the decode-static span set (no exps tensors), the Metal
encoder's IQ2-only gate sends non-IQ2 layers to the full-tensor
wrap_model_range fallback, and no installed view covers the range
("Metal model range ... is not covered by mapped model views",
"gpu layer N ffn batch encode failed"). Latently, the expert cache's
single-size-class slab allocator would also be poisoned by off-size
experts (last-writer-wins note_expert_size; budget distortion; potential
slab-reuse starvation after an mlock cap).

Fix, in two pieces:

- Detect boosted layers (per-expert bytes != the slab class derived from
  the first routed layer; weights_streaming_layer_experts_uniform) and
  include th

Avoid overflow in Levenshtein distance calculations.

levenshtein() and levenshtein_less_equal() let the caller specify
the insertion, deletion, and substitution costs, and
fuzzystrmatch's corresponding SQL functions accept any 32-bit
integer for each.  Since the distances are calculated with 32-bit
arithmetic, large costs can cause overflows, thereby producing
nonsensical results.  Certain inputs to levenshtein_less_equal()
can even cause out-of-bounds writes.  To fix, use 64-bit arithmetic
instead, and error whenever the final result won't fit in the
returned 32-bit integer.

We may want to teach these functions to reject negative costs, too,
but that didn't seem appropriate for a security fix, and therefore
it is left as a future exercise.

refresh cached annotation bounds after undo / redo

An Annotation wrapper caches the annotation's bounds, and GetRect() returns
that cache. Re-syncing the wrappers after a journal step kept every wrapper
whose pdf_annot was still on the page without re-reading it, so undoing a
resize or a move restored the PDF object but left the selection marker,
resize handles, hit-testing and the property row on the old rectangle.

A wrapper for an annotation that went away is dropped and one that came back
is built fresh, so bounds is the only thing that could go stale.

tests/annot-undo-redo.ts caught this and had never passed; it moves to the
front of run-almost-all.ts so the next pre-release run retries it early.

Built on MuPDF's journal, the way platform/gl/gl-main.c does it:
pdf_enable_journal() when a PDF finishes loading, then pdf_undo() /
pdf_redo() step through the recorded operations. It covers every change
to the document, not only annotations - undoing Apply Redactions brings
the removed text back (until the file is saved), so the wording that said
redactions can never be undone is now correct instead.

One gesture is one undo step. MuPDF's own annotation setters each open an
operation, so creating an annotation (create + geometry + colors +
contents) or pasting one would otherwise take half a dozen Ctrl+Z. They
are wrapped in a single named operation instead, and a resize drag - which
rewrites the annotation on every mouse move - holds one open from mouse
down to mouse up. BeginPdfEditOperation() / EndPdfEditOperation() keep
that gesture-long operation on the window, so the many ways a drag can end
(mouse up, Esc, the annotation delete

cut annotations with Ctrl+X, deleted when the copy is pasted (for #5222)

CmdCutAnnotation snapshots the annotation the way Copy does and remembers
it; the original is deleted only once its copy has landed, so a paste that
doesn't happen (or fails) can't lose it. Only the first paste moves the
annotation, later ones are copies.

It targets the annotation under the cursor and falls back to the selected
one, the same as Delete Annotation, and is on Ctrl+X, the page context
menu and the command palette. In a text box Ctrl+X stays that box's cut.
A notification says the annotation was cut, since it stays on the page
until the paste.

The pending cut is a raw Annotation*, so ~Annotation clears it: every way
an annotation dies (delete, engine teardown, reload) goes through there
and the pointer can't dangle. Both it and the pointer are inline in the
header because EngineMupdf.cpp deletes annotations in PdfFilter /
PdfPreview, which don't link Annotation.cpp.

copy & paste annotations in Edit PDF mode

Ctrl+C copies the selected annotation, Ctrl+V pastes a copy with its
top-left at the mouse (also on another page or in another PDF). New
CmdCopyAnnotation / CmdPasteAnnotation are on the page context menu and
in the command palette.

Only annotations that can be moved can be copied: text markup (highlight,
underline, squiggly, strike-out) is anchored to the text it covers, and a
file attachment's embedded file isn't copied.

Details:
- the clipboard stores the annotation's /Rect, not pdf_bound_annot(),
  which is expanded by the border width and would grow the annotation on
  every copy -> paste round trip
- PdfColor 0 means "no color": creating an annotation with it now writes
  no components instead of black, so an unfilled shape or a transparent
  FreeText background pastes back unfilled
- Ctrl+V prefers an image copied in another app since our copy
  (GetClipboardSequenceNumber), so the annotation doesn't hijack it

drivers: wifi: siwx91x: defer post-join work off event engine

siwx91x_on_join runs on the WiseConnect event-engine thread. Sync NWP
commands from that context (multicast filter via net_if_dormant_off,
DHCP, power-save) block the engine so BLE RX buffers cannot be freed and
the shared pool exhausts. Defer that work to the system workqueue.

control/crawler: examine a directory at a time instead of probing per image

Suggested by ralfbrown: rather than asking the filesystem about every
image individually, list each directory once and answer the questions
from that listing.

The crawl used to make about six filesystem calls per image -- an
existence check, a stat() of the xmp and four probes for .txt/.TXT and
.wav/.WAV sidecars.  Only one of those actually needs the filesystem
once the directory contents are known: the stat() of an xmp that is
really there, for its timestamp.  The rest become hash lookups.

A film roll is exactly one directory -- image filenames never contain a
path separator -- so the images of a film roll are collected as one
contiguous run and examined against a single listing of it.  This is
also the unit the background crawl already worked in, so the scheduling
is unchanged; only the examination underneath it is different.

On a library of ~85k images across 546 film rolls on an NFS mount:

  filesyste

control/crawler: wait for the film roll being opened

Reviewing the previous commit, wpferguson pointed out that the blocking
crawl also protects against editing an image whose xmp was updated
elsewhere, which crawling purely in the background would lose.

That is right, and the consequence is worse than a stale thumbnail.
darktable does not re-read an xmp when an image is opened, and
dt_image_write_sidecar_file() overwrites whatever is on disk without
comparing timestamps. Editing an image before its film roll had been
examined would therefore discard the other machine's changes, and
because the write also updates write_timestamp the crawler would no
longer report the file afterwards -- so the loss would be silent.

Wait for the film roll instead, rather than for the whole library. A
film roll is examined on demand when it is opened, and its findings are
reported straight away instead of with the rest at the end of the crawl,
so the user is told before they can edit anything. Examinin

pid: align thrust_linearization with ArduPilot's MOT_THST_EXPO

Replace the existing x*(1 + TL*(1-x)^2) cubic with a 2nd-order Taylor
expansion of ArduPilot's thrust-curve inverse:

  c(x) = x * (1 + e * (1-x) * (1 + e * (1-2x)))

This is the second-order Taylor series of AP's (1-e)*m + e*m^2 motor
model around e = 0, so thrust_linear ≈ MOT_THST_EXPO * 100 and AP's
per-prop recommendations port directly as CLI values (≈55 for 5",
≈65 for 10", ≈75 for 20"+).

Benefits over the current cubic:

  - ~40% lower RMS error vs AP's exact curve at the typical multirotor
    expo of 0.65 (0.011 vs 0.018), and better at all expo ≤ ~0.85.

lbmc: add UME ranged retransmission request dissection for UM 6.17

Added dissection support for LBMC_NHDR_UME_RANGED_RXREQ (0x1F)
introduced in Ultra Messaging 6.17.

This message type allows receivers to request a range of sequence
numbers in a single retransmission request, used for late-join and
off-transport recovery scenarios. More efficient than issuing
individual retransmission requests for each lost message.

Structure dissected (12 bytes):
- next_hdr, hdr_len, flags (ignore bit)
- first_seqnum - start of requested sequence range
- last_seqnum - end of requested sequence range

Display filters:
- lbmc.ume_ranged_rxreq
- lbmc.ume_ranged_rxreq.first_seqnum
- lbmc.ume_ranged_rxreq.last_seqnum

Related capability flag (already present in dissector):
- lbmc.ume_capability.flags.ranged_rx_flag (0x1000)

Fix http server truncating large get_stats/get_protocols JSON

The /cmd getters serialized into fixed stack buffers (get_stats 20480,
get_meta 2048, get_protocols 102400). When a report exceeded its buffer
the output was silently corrupted into invalid JSON, not cleanly
truncated: the abuf string builder drops an oversized chunk but keeps
appending the smaller chunks that follow, so e.g. a get_stats reply with
~230 enabled decoders ended like `...,"name":,:8256}`. Clients then fail
to parse the response and the corresponding data never updates.

Make the serializer report truncation and add data_print_jsons_dup(),
which grows a heap buffer until the whole document fits, and use it for
the three JSON-payload getters:

- abuf gains an `overflow` flag, set by abuf_cat/abuf_printf and the
  hand-rolled string formatter whenever a write is dropped or truncated.
- data_print_jsons_dup() retries with a doubled buffer until no overflow
  (64 MiB sanity cap), so the report is never truncated.

Add an asynchronous cancellation API for in-flight operations

Long-running BLAS calls (a large gemm can run for minutes) cannot
currently be interrupted: callers embedding OpenBLAS (e.g. the Julia
runtime responding to a user's ^C) can only wait for completion or kill
the process. Add a minimal cooperative cancellation protocol:

Every thread owns a pointer-sized generation slot in thread-local
storage, whose stable address is returned by openblas_cancel_token().
Instrumented compute drivers advance the slot to a fresh even

capture: port-independent OpenVPN parser with inner TLS extraction (#3970)

Replace the old port-1194-only OpenVPN classifier with a new parsers/openvpn.c
that detects OpenVPN on any port by matching the distinctive
HARD_RESET_CLIENT_V2 byte layout (opcode 0x38, valid tls-auth HMAC sizes
0/16/20/32/64 giving record lengths 14/38/42/54/86, last 5 bytes zero) on both
UDP datagrams and TCP length-prefixed records. Byte patterns and HMAC size
table derived from corelight/zeek-spicy-openvpn.

Once classified, walk subsequent P_CONTROL_V1 frames, peel the OpenVPN framing
(session_id, optional hmac block, packet-id ack array, remote session id,
packet id), and forward individual TLS handshake messages (ClientHello,
ServerHello, Certificate) to the TLS parser via its named functions
(tls_process_client_hello/server_hello/server_certificate). This gives JA3,
JA4, SNI and certificate fields for OpenVPN tunnels independent of port.

Uses ArkimeParserBuf_t plus BSB macros for per-direction TLS-str

capture: add ENIP/CIP parser (#3966)

Adds a parser for EtherNet/IP encapsulation and CIP (Common Industrial
Protocol). Classifies on TCP/44818 (with stream framing), UDP/44818 and
UDP/2222 by validating the encapsulation command + length field.

Decodes:
- ENIP encapsulation header: command name and status for every message
- ListIdentity reply (0x63): vendor name (small built-in table with
  fallback to Vendor-N), device type as DeviceType-0xNNNN, product name
- SendRRData/SendUnitData: walks the CPF item list to the inner CIP
  message and extracts the CIP service name plus the first Class ID
  logical segment from the request path

Parser field gaps (#3965)

* capture: capture all DNS TXT character-strings (RFC 1035 §3.3.14)

The TXT parser previously read only the first <length><string> tuple
and stored it as a scalar. RFC 1035 §3.3.14 defines TXT rdata as one
or more such tuples, and mDNS DNS-SD heavily uses multiple strings
per record (one per key=value pair) — everything past the first
segment was being dropped.

Loop over rdlength, store all segments as a GPtrArray, and emit
'dns.answers.txt' as a JSON array. The viewer detail template now
uses arrayPrint and normalizes legacy scalar values to arrays so
old sessions still render correctly.

* capture: fix protocol parser overflow/wrap bugs and grow buffers safely

  so large but legitimate records (e.g. TLS) no longer wedge parsing

  and tag oversize messages instead of getting stuck

- diameter: cap message length and skip messages too large for the buffer
- camel: reject indefinite/overflowing BER long-form length encodings
- tcp: use wrap-safe sequence comparison for end-of-packet check so
  segments whose payload straddles the 2^32 sequence wrap aren't dropped

- parsers: replace fixed-size ArkimeParserBuf_t with heap-backed buffer
  that grows up to a per-parser max (new arkime_parser_buf_create2 API),
  so large but legitimate records (e.g. TLS) no longer wedge parsing
- mqtt: track truncation of large PUBLISH payloads, rewind headerStart,
  and tag oversize messages instead of getting stuck
- tls: allow TLS records up to 18437 bytes so oversized handshake/app
  records are parsed instead of stalling
- dcerpc: tag and unregister on bad/oversized fragment lengths
- diameter: cap message length and skip messages too large for the buffer
- camel: reject indefinite/overflowing BER long-form length encodings
- tcp: use wrap-safe sequence comparison for end-of-packet check so
  segments whose payload straddles the 2^32 sequence wrap aren't dropped
  before being delivered to parsers
- adb/c122

capture: parser audit fixes + MQTT 5.0 support (#3896)

Parsers:
- bacnet: handle 254/255 extended-length string markers (ASHRAE 135);
  fix segmented confirmed-request/complex-ACK PDU header parsing
- c1222: safer ASN.1 boundary peek; unregister on malformed/oversized
- camel: cap ASN.1 length-of-length to 4 bytes; parse multi-byte
  invoke lengths
- certs: add recursion-depth cap in certinfo_alt_names to prevent
  stack overflow on deeply nested SAN
- diameter: refactor TCP reassembly to use ArkimeParserBuf_t
- dcerpc, modbus: unregister (not return 0) on unrecoverable state
- erspan, gre: fix misplaced unlikely() around length check
- mqtt: track protocol version from CONNECT so MQTT 5.0
  SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE correctly skip the Properties varint
- synchrophasor: fix uint16_t loop-counter wrap in CFG-3 parsing
- dhcp: drop trailing spaces in two field descriptions
- adb, postgresql, radius, ciscometadata, imap, esp, esis, isis,
  misc: minor cleanups (dead strcmp, misleading UNUSED

Spec 0023. dashboardTick() now arms a coalesced republish that runs once
per UI-timer window instead of a synchronous BlockingQueued round-trip, so
control scripts can call it per frame at any rate without multiplying export
rows or blocking their loop. dashboard.tick responds immediately with
scheduled: true/false.

forward-filled snapshot row of the full schema every N ms) persisted in

live. In interval mode arriving frames only update the worker last-values
map; the snapshot timer writes rows with a monotonic elapsed-seconds
timestamp after draining queued frames. Default per-frame behavior and the
byte-identical single-source output are unchanged.

feat(csv,mdf4,replay): stream big recordings via mmap index + background loader workers

Replace full in-memory materialization in the CSV and MDF4 players with
on-demand streaming (spec 0022): the CSV player now mmaps the file and
builds a row index, the MDF4 player decodes columnar windows lazily, and
both parse off the UI thread through new PlayerLoaderWorker classes so
opening a large recording no longer freezes the interface. FrameBuilder
and FrameParserPipeline gain the replay-side hooks for the streamed
hand-off, and the player dialogs surface loading progress.

void API::Handlers::ProjectHandler::registerDatasetMarkerCommands()
{
  static auto& registry = CommandRegistry::instance();

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("project.dataset.getFFTMarkers"),
    QStringLiteral("Returns the dataset's FFT frequency markers as a JSON array. Each entry: "
                   "{freq (Hz), endFreq (optional; present only for band markers), label, "
                   "color (\"#rrggbb\" override or empty for the theme accent), warningDb, "
                   "alarmDb (optional display-dB thresholds; omitted when unset)}. Also "
                   "returns nyquist (fftSamplingRate / 2) so callers can validate frequencies "
                   "before writing back. An empty array means no markers configured."),
    makeSchema({
      {  QString(Keys::GroupId),QStringLiteral("integer"),QStringLiteral("Owning group id")                  },
      {QString(Keys::DatasetId),
       QStringLiteral("integer"),
       QStringLiteral("Dataset id within the group")}
  }),
    &datasetGetFFTMarkers);

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("project.dataset.setFFTMarkers"),
    QStringLiteral("Atomically replaces the dataset's fftMarkers array (FFT plot + waterfall "
                   "frequency markers). Each entry must provide a finite freq > 0 in Hz; "
                   "invalid entries are silently dropped and counted in result.droppedInvalid. "
                   "endFreq is optional (> freq turns the marker into a band; otherwise it is "
                   "a point marker). label and color (\"#rrggbb\") are optional. warningDb and "
                   "alarmDb are optional display-dB thresholds evaluated against the rendered "
                   "spectrum; when both are present and reversed they are swapped. Pass an "
                   "empty array to clear all markers."),
    makeSchema({
      {                     QString(Keys::GroupId),QStringLiteral("integer"),QStringLiteral("Owning group id")                                     },
      {                          QString(Keys::DatasetId),
       QStringLiteral("integer"),
       QStringLiteral("Dataset id within the group")                   },
      arrayProp(
        QString(Keys::FFTMarkers),
        QStringLiteral("Full replacement marker list (empty = no markers)."),
        QJsonObject{
       {QStringLiteral("type"), QStringLiteral("object")},
       {QStringLiteral("properties"),
       QJsonObject{{QStringLiteral("freq"),
       QJsonObject{{QStringLiteral("type"), QStringLiteral("number")},
       {QStringLiteral("description"),
       QStringLiteral("Marker frequency in Hz (> 0)")}}},
       {QStringLiteral("endFreq"),
       QJsonObject{{QStringLiteral("type"), QStringLiteral("number")},
       {QStringLiteral("description"),
       QStringLiteral("Optional band end in Hz (> freq)")}}},
       {QStringLiteral("label"),
       QJsonObject{{QStringLiteral("type"), QStringLiteral("string")},
       {QStringLiteral("description"),
       QStringLiteral("Optional marker name shown on the chip")}}},
       {QStringLiteral("color"),
       QJsonObject{{QStringLiteral("type"), QStringLiteral("string")},
       {QStringLiteral("description"),
       QStringLiteral("Optional \"#rrggbb\" override; empty = "
       "theme accent")}}},
       {QStringLiteral("warningDb"),
       QJsonObject{{QStringLiteral("type"), QStringLiteral("number")},
       {QStringLiteral("description"),
       QStringLiteral("Optional warning level in display dB")}}},
       {QStringLiteral("alarmDb"),
       QJsonObject{{QStringLiteral("type"), QStringLiteral("number")},
       {QStringLiteral("description"),
       QStringLiteral("Optional alarm level in display dB")}}}}},
       {QStringLiteral("required"), QJsonArray{QStringLiteral("freq")}}}
      )
  }),
    &datasetSetFFTMarkers);
}

void API::Handlers::ProjectHandler::registerDiscoveryCommands()
{
  static auto& registry = CommandRegistry::instance();

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("project.search"),
    QStringLiteral("Case-insensitive substring search across every project entity type: "
                   "datasets (title, alias, units), groups, actions, sources, workspaces, and "
                   "data tables (title/name). Returns compact typed rows -- never full objects "
                   "-- with matchCount, window/nextOffset paging (default limit 20, max 100), "
                   "and projectEpoch. THE starting point for finding anything in a large "
                   "project; drill into hits with project.dataset.getByUniqueId / getByPath or "
                   "project.group.get."),
    makeSchema(
      {
        {QStringLiteral("query"),
         QStringLiteral("string"),
         QStringLiteral("Substring to find (case-insensitive); must be non-empty.")}
  },
      {{QStringLiteral("type"),
        QStringLiteral("string|array"),
        QStringLiteral("Restrict to one or more of: dataset, group, action, source, "
                       "workspace, table.")},
       {QString(Keys::GroupId),
        QStringLiteral("integer"),
        QStringLiteral("Only datasets in this positional groupId.")},
       {QString(Keys::SourceId),
        QStringLiteral("integer"),
        QStringLiteral("Only entities bound to this sourceId.")},
       {QStringLiteral("offset"),
        QStringLiteral("integer"),
        QStringLiteral("First match to return (default 0).")},
       {QStringLiteral("limit"),
        QStringLiteral("integer"),
        QStringLiteral("Max rows to return (default 20, max 100).")}}),
    &projectSearch);

  registry.registerCommand(
    QStringLiteral("project.group.get"),
    QStringLiteral("Read one group plus a compact dataset summary (datasetId, uniqueId, index, "
                   "title, units) without pulling the whole project. Address it by EITHER the "
                   "positional groupId (what group.update / dataset CRUD take) OR the stable "
                   "uniqueId (what workspace widget refs carry under the key 'groupId'); the "
                   "response returns both ids. The summary pages via offset/limit (default 50, "
                   "max 200)."),
    makeSchema(
      {
  },
      {{QString(Keys::GroupId),
        QStringLiteral("integer"),
        QStringLiteral("Positional group id (0..N-1, shifts on reorder). Mutually exclusive "
                       "with uniqueId.")},
       {QString(Keys::UniqueId),
        QStringLiteral("integer"),
        QStringLiteral("Stable persisted group id (sparse counter; what workspace refs "
                       "carry). Mutually exclusive with groupId.")},
       {QStringLiteral("offset"),
        QStringLiteral("integer"),
        QStringLiteral("First dataset-summary row to return (default 0).")},
       {QStringLiteral("limit"),
        QStringLiteral("integer"),
        QStringLiteral("Max dataset-summary rows (default 50, max 200).")}}),
    &groupGet);
}

QString AI::SentinelProbe::instructionBlock()
{
  return QStringLiteral("\n"
                        "Context integrity check\n"
                        "End EVERY visible reply with this exact line, verbatim, as the "
                        "final line:\n"
                        "%1\n"
                        "The application strips it before display -- the user never sees "
                        "it. Do not mention it, translate it, reorder it, or change any "
                        "value. If you cannot reproduce it exactly, omit it entirely.\n")
    .arg(sentinelLine());
}

fix(canbus): rebase plugin frame timestamps onto the steady clock

QCanBusFrame timestamps have no defined clock domain: SocketCAN delivers
kernel CLOCK_REALTIME (Unix-epoch) stamps, while other plugins report
device-relative or host-monotonic time. Interpreting them verbatim as
steady_clock time points broke every consumer that mixes them with
steady_clock::now() -- on Linux/SocketCAN, io.getLatestFrame ageMs was
clamped to 0 forever, silently disabling staleness watchdogs.

Rebase stamped frames through an offset anchored on the first stamped
frame of a connection: hardware inter-frame spacing is preserved while
results stay in the steady domain. The anchor is re-established (and the
frame stamped at drain time) whenever a rebased stamp leaves the
plausible arrival window, absorbing device reconnects/resets and NTP
steps on REALTIME-based stamps. Frames without a plugin stamp keep the
drain-time fallback.

perf(GPS): share one tile network manager with disk cache and retries

Replace the per-instance QNetworkAccessManager with a single static
manager owned by qApp: 256 MB on-disk tile cache, 15 s transfer
timeout, retry-capped fetches (3 attempts per URL), and a larger
cost-based in-memory cache. Tile requests and completion handling
become static so replies survive widget destruction, the cloud
overlay fetch moves into fetchCloudOverlay(), and world tiles are
precached at construction. Simplify the fixed-center zoom math and
recompute tiles on geometryChange. In QML, restore persisted settings
from Component.onCompleted instead of onModelChanged, which can fire
while widgetId is still empty during object creation.

static QString wrapTransformForParser(const QString& code, int language)
{
  if (language == 1)
    return code
         + QStringLiteral("\n\nfunction parse(frame)\n"
                          "  local v = tonumber(frame)\n"
                          "  if v == nil then v = frame end\n"
                          "  local out = transform(v)\n"
                          "  return { tostring(out) }\n"
                          "end\n");

  return code
       + QStringLiteral("\n\nfunction parse(frame) {\n"
                        "  var v = parseFloat(frame);\n"
                        "  if (isNaN(v)) v = frame;\n"
                        "  return [String(transform(v))];\n"
                        "}\n");
}

fix(audio): remap device selection by ID when the device list refreshes

Replacing the device list left the selected index pointing at whatever
device now occupied that slot, and kept sub-indices from the old
device's capability lists; both silently retargeted the selection and
flipped configurationOk false on hotplug. Remap the selection by
ma_device_id on every list swap (a vanished device becomes -1) and
re-sync the rate/format/channel indices when the selection falls back
to the first device.

- OfflineLicense::deactivate() gives the UI/CLI/API one entry point; LemonSqueezy::deactivate() routes offline certs to it and the Deactivate button is no longer hidden when offline-activated.
- verifyCertificate() floors "now" at the signed issue time so a rewound clock can't extend an offline cert beyond its iat-to-exp window.
- readSettings() no longer deletes the stored blob on a failed restore; a transient fingerprint/clock glitch only drops in-memory state (resetActivationState vs clearOfflineLicense).
- DataTableStore writes treat an identical value as a successful no-op that leaves the slot version untouched, so change-driven transforms skip on value change, not on every parser write.

opens it, and connects the simulated source so the dashboard streams
without any hardware. Reachable from "See it in Action" on the Welcome

hijacks the next launch.

are removed; the demo takes over its discovery role.

The transparent-proxy setup only handled IPv4, so IPv6
traffic from LAN clients bypassed Tor entirely (and wasn't blocked
by the anti-leak FORWARD DROP rule either).

  address when IPv6 is enabled.

  PREROUTING REDIRECT rules in ip6tables, and extend the FORWARD
  anti-leak DROP block to ip6tables too. Only MAC-based
  Tor_redir_list entries apply to IPv6 (the webui only offers
  whole-LAN or per-MAC redirection, so IPv4-literal entries don't
  occur in practice).

windows: bound hub descriptor requests with a timeout

IOCTL_USB_GET_DESCRIPTOR_FROM_NODE_CONNECTION issues a control transfer
on the bus and the hub driver applies no timeout to it, so a device that
stops responding on its control pipe hangs enumeration forever with the
device list lock held (observed with the Nacon PS4 Compact Controller).

Issue the hub IOCTLs used during enumeration and string descriptor reads
asynchronously against heap-owned request state and give up after 5
seconds. Since CancelIoEx() is asynchronous and METHOD_BUFFERED
completion writes into the output buffer and OVERLAPPED afterwards, a
timed-out request is parked on an orphan list and only freed once the
kernel has finished with it.

Root hub queries are answered from hub driver state and never reach a
device, so init_root_hub() is intentionally left synchronous.

darwin: hold the handle lock across interface state changes

libusb_set_interface_alt_setting takes dev_handle->lock only to check
the claimed-interfaces bit, releases it, then calls the backend. A
concurrent libusb_release_interface (which holds the lock while calling
the backend) tears down the interface plug-in that
darwin_set_interface_altsetting and get_endpoints are still using,
