Handle RNN activation parameters safely (#31675)

This pull request prevents out-of-bounds reads of RNN activation
parameters while preserving ONNX-spec-legal attribute lists.

**RNN activation parameter handling:**

* Reuses the shared `rnn::detail::ActivationFuncs` normalization already
used by ORT's LSTM and GRU kernels.
* Consumes `activation_alpha` and `activation_beta` values only for
activation functions that require them.
* Applies activation-specific ONNX defaults when a required value is
absent, including `LeakyRelu`, `HardSigmoid`, and `Elu` defaults.
* Safely accepts empty, shorter, and longer parameter lists without
indexing those lists by direction.

**Unit test coverage:**

* Verifies mixed activations consume only the required alpha and beta
values.
* Verifies empty parameter attributes use activation-specific defaults.
* Verifies a missing `LeakyRelu` alpha uses the ONNX default of `0.01`.
* Verifies extra alpha and beta entries are safely ignored.

Fix TfIdfVectorizer weight indexing semantics (#31649)

This pull request refactors the `TfIdfVectorizer` implementation to
improve the handling of n-gram index mapping, especially for cases where
n-gram indexes are not sequential or are permuted. The changes also
update the weighting callback signature to provide more context, and add
new tests to ensure correct behavior for permuted n-gram indexes.

### Refactoring and API Changes

* Updated the signature of the `fn_weight` callback in
`TfIdfVectorizer::ComputeImpl` to take both the n-gram id and output
index, allowing for more flexible and accurate mapping between n-gram
ids and output vector indices.
* Modified all usages of `fn_weight` in `ComputeImpl` to pass both the
n-gram id and output index, ensuring the callback has the necessary
information to apply weights correctly.

[WebGPU EP] Support int64 for Min and Max (#31709)

### Description
Registers the WebGPU Min and Max kernels with conditional int64 support,
mirroring the existing Add/Sub/Equal int64 mechanism. The kernels were
previously registered with `WebGpuSupportedNumberTypes()` (float/fp16/
int32/uint32 only), causing int64 tensors to fall back to CPU.

### Motivation and Context
Min/Max are arithmetic/comparison ops, so they reuse the existing
low-32-bit i32 shader path (like Add/Sub). Values outside the int32
range produce incorrect results, which is acceptable for token-position
workloads and consistent with the other arithmetic int64 kernels.

`int64` support is gated behind the enableInt64 provider option, so the
generic `Min_12_Int64`/`Max_12_Int64` tests do not exercise it. Added
WebGPU int64 tests (int64 enabled, CPU-EP fallback disabled) mirroring
the Add int64 path coverage, element-wise, size divisible by 4, scalar
operand, broadcast, plus the variadic (>2 input) fold unique to Min/M

Wire max-shape inference into workspace estimation (#31613)

### Description

This PR wires estimation-only input-shape hints into the two-level
workspace-estimation flow described in #29775.

It adds the `session.max_shape_override` session option:

```text
input_ids:[8,4096];attention_mask:[8,4096]
```

ORT validates the configured graph-input shapes before cloning, applies
them to a disposable shadow graph, runs recursive shape inference, and
captures concrete intermediate `NodeArg` shapes without changing runtime
input constraints or executable-graph metadata.

The resolved shapes are consumed at:

- **Level 1:** CUDA `MatMulNBits` workspace estimation during
`GetCapability()`.
- **Level 2:** `DeclareWorkspaceRequirements()` on constructed kernels
during `FinalizeSessionState()`.

Static graph shapes remain usable at Level 2 without configuring an
override. Nodes whose inputs remain unresolved retain the existing
dynamic allocation/estimation fallback.

Minimize telemetry context and modernize 1DS integration (#29872)

## Summary

Minimizes automatic POSIX/1DS common context and makes telemetry an
explicit build opt-out on supported native targets.

## Context minimization

- Removes the unused POSIX `ProviderOptions` emitter.
- Suppresses duplicate app name, app/user locale, timezone, and enrolled
tenant ID.
- Retains `ext.net.*` on `ProcessInfo`, then clears it best-effort
before later events.
- Removes redundant POSIX `processName` and `LibraryName` fields.
- Retains ORT correlation, version, framework, device, timestamp,
sampling, and SDK-ordering fields.
- Keeps optional context suppression non-fatal and retries network
cleanup until it succeeds.
- Preserves canonical event names without adding an `ORT` or
`OnnxRuntime` prefix.

## Build behavior

- Replaces the opt-in `--use_telemetry` interface with the opt-out
`--no_telemetry` flag.
- Enables telemetry by default for supported Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS,
and Android targets.

Validate constant tensor byte size in DML OnnxTensorWrapper (#31665)

### Description
<!-- Describe your changes. -->
Adds a bounds check to the DML EP's `OnnxTensorWrapper` so that a
`TensorProto` whose declared shape implies more data than its backing
buffer actually holds is rejected at construction, instead of being
handed to operator kernels.

- New helper `VerifyTensorProtoFitsInBuffer` in
`MLOperatorAuthorImpl.cpp` computes the byte size implied by the
tensor's dims and element type, and fails with `E_INVALIDARG` when the
buffer is smaller
- Called at the end of the `OnnxTensorWrapper` constructor, covering the
`raw_data`, typed-field, and external-data paths
- Adds `onnxruntime/test/providers/dml_onnx_tensor_wrapper_test.cc` with
positive / negative cases.

### Motivation and Context

DML reliability improvement.

the gated-delta

decay = decay_scale * Softplus(a + dt_bias)
beta  = Sigmoid(b)                            # optional second output
```

`dt_bias` and `decay_scale` are float32 per-head vectors of length `H`;
`decay_scale` is the

**`com.microsoft::GatedRMSNorm`**

WebGPU EP: Add uint8 support to Gather kernel (#29861)

### Description
The WebNN EP maps ONNX BOOL → WebNN uint8. When WebNN uses WebGPU as its
backend, a Gather on a bool tensor (e.g., in
[detr-resnet-50](https://huggingface.co/Xenova/detr-resnet-50/blob/main/onnx/model_fp16.onnx))
is lowered to WebGPU Gather on uint8, which previously had no matching
kernel.



### Motivation and Context
Models such as detr-resnet-50 use Gather on bool tensors. The WebNN EP
converts bool to uint8 before dispatching to the WebGPU backend, so the
WebGPU Gather kernel must accept uint8 to handle this path end-to-end.

kernel, making the effective dispatch cascade **cuDNN → Flash → MEA →

fp16/bf16, `cudnn_sdpa::is_supported`. Not built-guarded (relies on the
wrapper's `CUDNN_MAJOR` stubs + `is_stable()`)

item that had been playing. The position then indexed a list that no longer
contained it, and the next item to play was computed from it: GetNextItemIdx
returned m_iCurrentSong + 1, which is past the end of a list repopulated from

report is against that method: clear the playlist while a video plays, queue
another item, and the queued item is never reached.

one, so clearing the music playlist cannot disturb a video that is

fixed: quote the parameters Addons.ExecuteAddon hands to an add-on

The array and string forms of the params argument were escaped with
StringUtils::Paramify before being formatted into the RunAddon builtin; the object
form was concatenated raw. CUtil::SplitParams ends a parameter at any comma not
inside quotes, so an object value containing one arrived at the add-on as two
arguments, and a value containing a double quote or a backslash corrupted the
arguments that followed it. The object form is the one the method's own
documentation shows, so this is the common path rather than a corner.

Quote the assembled "key=value" pair rather than the value alone, so a comma in the
key is covered as well. SplitParams strips the surrounding quotes again on the way
out, so a caller whose keys and values contain none of these characters sees no
change.

The patch version covers both JSON-RPC behaviour changes on this branch: the schema
is unaltered, and each method now does what it already declare

fixed: honour the declared wait parameter of Addons.ExecuteAddon

The method declares three parameters - addonid, params and wait - but the handler
read "wait" out of the params object rather than from the parameters themselves, so
the declared one was never consulted. The blocking branch was unreachable through
the documented API and the method always answered before the add-on had done
anything, while a caller who happened to pass a "wait" key inside params got the
blocking behaviour, plus a spurious wait= argument handed to the add-on.

The receiver changed from the parameter object to the params object in 9e9396b073,
which split ExecBuiltIn into SendMsg and PostMsg; nothing else in that commit
touched this method, so the parameter has been inert since Kodi 16.

The parameter handling moves into ParseExecuteAddonParams so it can be tested
without the add-on manager or the application messenger. The handler still resolves
the add-on id itself, because that needs neither.

fixed: read ID3 tags from .mp2 files

.mp2 is a recognised music extension, so Kodi lists and plays MPEG-1 Layer II files happily, but
two separate hard-coded extension lists decide whether a tag is read and neither of them names it.
CMusicInfoTagLoaderFactory::CreateLoader returns no loader for the extension, and
CTagLoaderTagLib::Load has no case that opens one, so the file reaches the library with no title,
artist or album.

Renaming the file to .mp3 was the only workaround available, and that it works is the whole
argument: TagLib's MPEG reader parses Layer II exactly as it parses Layer III, so the extension
was the only thing standing in the way. Both lists now name mp2.

by tools/testdata/mkmp2.py rather than encoded from audio, so it stays a few kilobytes and holds
only what the test is about.

changed: release the extension lists on deinitialization and guard the getters

CFileExtensionProvider is constructed with the service manager and stays reachable
through the service broker until the process ends, but Deinitialize drops the advanced
settings that its lazily built extension lists read. Every list is built on first read,
so the first cold Get*Extensions call after deinitialization dereferenced null - and
such calls are routine: one-argument URIUtils::GetExtension and HasExtension consult
GetCompoundArchiveExtensions for any path containing a dot. A long session rarely sees
it, because some earlier call has already built the list and a warm list is returned
without touching the settings.

settings that have gone, and the getters answer an empty string and log rather than
reading a list they cannot build. An empty answer is what a caller can act on: it is

test: cover Matroska tag reading through both readers

Three layers, because that is where the faults were: a name mapped to
the wrong field, a reader disagreeing with the other about the same
file, and tags landing on the wrong track.

MatroskaTagMapping is pinned first - the spaced spellings mp3tag writes,
the comma delimited role pairs, and a name read against its level, since
every caller depends on a name keeping one meaning.

Two of its cases exist because the values a reader hands over are not
always the values a file carried: a repeat joined with the spaced
delimiter, split back apart on a list holding "/", used to keep the
delimiter's spaces, and an album level ARTIST used to reach SetArtist()
joined with a delimiter it does not split on. nolevel.mka names its
Segment differently from the TITLE its tags carry, so that a file stating
its own title is told from a container naming itself - with both spelled
the same way, nothing said which of them the album was named after.

feat(music): read Matroska tags through a reader that TagLib or FFmpeg backs

Reading Matroska tags unconditionally included <taglib/matroska*.h>,
which exists only from TagLib 2.2, while required_deps asks for
TagLib>=1.9.0. Anything older fails to build, and 2.2 and 2.3 build but
crash on a malformed seek head, so a packager without a 2.3.1 package had
no working configuration at all. An unpatched 2.3.1 is no better: it
defines the API and then reads nothing from any Matroska over 512 KiB, so
TagLibVersion.h says the floor covers the patched library only, and that
it moves to 2.3.2 rather than growing a runtime workaround.

CMatroskaTagReader is the only way to either library and the only place a
version macro is read; the reader is chosen at preprocess time from
TAGLIB_*_VERSION, which also settles system against internal TagLib
without threading a cache variable through core_require_dep. Below the
floor Matroska tags come from FFmpeg's demuxer rather than disappearing,
and the FFmp

Opening a game that more than one emulator can play asks which one to use,
and asks again next time, and the time after that. Disc images are the worst
of it, since .bin/.cue is claimed by the Saturn, PSX, Dreamcast, Sega CD and
PC Engine CD cores at once, so a folder of Saturn games means answering the
same question forever.

Remember the answer instead. One table says "this path uses this emulator",
where the path is either a game or a folder holding games. A game is asked
for first and only then the folder above it, and the folder above that, which
is what makes a choice made on one game an override of the folder it sits in:
point a Saturn folder at YabaSanshiro and the one disc that needs Beetle can
still say so.

A remembered emulator is a preference rather than an instruction, and is only
used if it can still open the game in front of it. A folder has no idea what

refactor(music): extract the Matroska tag name mapping

Deciding which CMusicInfoTag field a Matroska tag name means was written
inside CMusicInfoTagLoaderMatroska, where CAudioBookFileDirectory could
not reach it and kept a second reading of the same names.

MatroskaTagMapping holds it once, and a tag's level travels beside its
name rather than inside it: only both together say which field a name
means - an ARTIST at album level is the album's, at track level the
song's - and the album's stands in for the song's until the song says
otherwise.

Repeated SimpleTags arrive concatenated into one delimited value, and
SetArtist() splits what it is handed on the user's musicitemseparator
from advancedsettings.xml. The two only agree at the default setting, so
MapTag() splits ARTIST on the delimiter a reader joins with - named once
as MatroskaTagMapping::MultiValueSeparator - and rejoins with the user's.
Splitting on the caller's whole separator list instead would take "/"
along and make two

refactor(filesystem): open a file for FFmpeg in one place

Opening a CFile, allocating an FFmpeg buffer, wiring the AVIO callbacks
and unwinding whatever was reached on failure is written out by hand in
CMusicCodecInfoFFmpeg and in CAudioBookFileDirectory, and the copies have
drifted: one sizes its buffer from the chunk size and the other fixes it,
one tells FFmpeg when the file cannot seek and the other does not, one
caps the packet size. CFFmpegVfsContext does it once and closes the three
in order when it goes, which is the part every failure path had to
remember.

The settled behaviour is the widest of what the copies did: a buffer of
at least 32KiB, or the file's chunk size where that is larger, the
seekable flag taken from IOControl and a packet size matching the buffer.

The callers move over in the commits that follow.

engine: support up to 4 additional shadowless directional lights (#10248)

* engine: support up to 4 additional shadowless directional lights

Allow a scene to contain up to CONFIG_MAX_EXTRA_DIRECTIONAL_LIGHTS (4)
directional lights in addition to the dominant one; the additional
lights are evaluated without shadows. The dominant directional light
(highest intensity) behaves as before: it owns slot 0 of the light
SoA, cascaded shadow maps and the sun disc. Directional lights beyond
the cap are ignored, preserving the previous dominant-light selection
semantics as the degenerate case.

The feature is automatic and adds no cost to the common single-light
case: a new dynamic specialization constant
(RUNTIME_CONFIG_HAS_EXTRA_DIRECTIONAL_LIGHTS, following the
RUNTIME_CONFIG_HAS_DYNAMIC_LIGHTING pattern) is set per view when the
scene contains more than one directional light, so the extra lights
loop compiles away entirely in programs specialized for single-light
scenes.

- Scene: FScene::pr

implements EVSSM (a.k.a. PCSS with EVSM) (#10188)

* implements EVSSM (a.k.a. PCSS with EVSM)

PCSS is typically extremely expensive due to the large number of
samples required for blocker search and shadow blurring.

By leveraging EVSM, we can achieve PCSS with a handful of samples. This
improves performance significantly on the shadow sampling side.
Of course, we pay a price on the shadow map generation side, since
EVSM is typically 2 to 4 times slower.

With this change, we deprecate and remove support for DPCF, which
doesn't make sense anymore. It was expensive and low quality.


RDIFF_ACCEPT_NEW_GOLDENS
SIZEGUARD_BYPASS

libstore: add a minimal derivation builder for Windows

buildLocally threw UnimplementedError("building derivations is not yet
implemented on Windows"). This replaces it with a working but deliberately small
builder, so nix build does something on Windows.

Verified end to end under Wine 11.0: nix.exe builds a derivation whose builder is
cmd.exe, registers the output in a Windows store, and the built binary then runs.

canonicalisation, and nix path-info reports it valid with the right deriver. A

libutil: implement getEnv in terms of getEnvOs

getEnv used getenv, which reads the C runtime's copy of the environment. That
copy is snapshotted at process start and setEnv does not update it, because
setEnv goes through SetEnvironmentVariable and writes the Win32 block. So on
Windows getEnv could not see anything the process itself had set, and reported a
variable absent that getEnvOs reported present.

Per review this is not a Windows special case: getEnv always goes through
getEnvOs, and each platform implements getEnvOs against its own primitive.

That needed the Unix delegation inverted as well. getEnvOs there was defined as
return getEnv(key), so making the shared getEnv call getEnvOs would have recursed
forever. getEnvOs is now the primitive on both platforms: getenv on Unix, the
Win32 block on Windows. OsString is std::string on Unix, so the conversions are
identity and behaviour there is unchanged.

libutil: treat an existing empty environment variable as empty, not absent

getEnvOs returned nullopt when the second GetEnvironmentVariableW stored zero
characters. But reaching that call means the sizing call succeeded, which means
the variable exists, so zero there means the value is empty rather than missing.

Windows distinguishes the two: an existing empty variable returns 1 from the
sizing call and 0 from the buffered one, while an absent one returns 0 from both
and sets ERROR_ENVVAR_NOT_FOUND. Unix already gets this right, so the same
calling code took different branches on the two platforms, and one consequence
is that an empty-string guard in FileTransferSettings is unreachable on Windows.

The branch is gone rather than corrected: resize(resultSize) on a zero count
gives the empty string, and returning it gives an engaged optional.

Tests pass under Wine at 785 and natively at 807; emptyValueIsPresent fails on
Windows without this change.

libstore: check fixed-output derivation paths against their content address

The output path stated in the ATerm for a fixed-output derivation is
redundant --- it is a function of the content address --- and we were
simply discarding it while parsing. This meant bogus paths were not
getting caught, and they would also cause a round-trip violation.

Now, we instead assert that the path is correct. We compute the path as
the unparser does, and reject a mismatch.

This requires threading the derivation name and output name into
`parseOutput`, and so also into `readOutput` for the wire protocol,
which had the same gap.

The check is compiled out under `FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION`,
which our fuzz builds define project-wide. Unlike the other
canonicality checks on this branch --- sorted keys, no redundant escapes
--- which a fuzzer can learn to satisfy, this one asks it to produce a
hash preimage, so keeping it would make the fixed-output branch
unreachable to the fuzzer rather

libstore/derivation: Split hash modulo out of the ATerm format

`derivation/aterm.{hh,cc}` was carrying two topics: the ATerm encoding
of a derivation, and the hash-modulo computation defined over it. Now,
move the latter to `derivation/modulo.{hh,cc}` and put it in a new
`nix::derivation::modulo` (sub) namespace, changing identifiers
accordingly.

When I split out those files in 7d4eb33c21f421d9c25ec2636250722dd063a1ed
I thought putting both things in there was fine, but now I no longer think
it is, and we need to separate concerns even more. The unit tests really
want it.

The one thing the two files must share is the unparser for the
intermediate form, so the formerly-`static` `unparseDerivation` becomes
a public `unparse` overload in `aterm.hh`, explicitly instantiated in
`aterm.cc` for the `modulo::Inputs` cases. `aterm.hh` only forward
declares `modulo::Inputs`, so it does not depend on `modulo.hh`.

libstore: Expose `unparseModulo`, characterize it in tests

As expressed elsewhere, I like characterization tests best because they
make our testsuite somewhat implementation-agnostic. In a world where
many people are reimplementing Nix, this is useful for them, and ideally
a truly implementation-agnostic test suite would move us towards having
a ratified (like IETF) specification.

In the case of `hashModulo`, the interesting thing to test is the
"derivation modulo inputs" that is normally never *seen* --- it the
preimage to the hash that is thrown away. Crucial data that is usually
not visible is a perfect candidate for a characterization test, so we
make sure to to expose what we need in order to write that test.

The test graph mirrors the reproducer in #16307. When the next commit
fixes the bug, having the tests in place already will make it easier to
review.

Add Power-of-Two-Choices Peak-EWMA load balancer (p2c) (#3367)

* Add Power-of-Two-Choices Peak-EWMA load balancer (p2c)

Implements the p2c load balancing policy proposed in #3340: each
selection samples two random servers (configurable via choices=N) and
routes to the lower peak-EWMA latency * (inflight+1) / weight score.
Upward latency spikes take effect immediately while recovery decays
over tau_ms (default 10s), so a degraded server is shed within one
observation at O(1) selection cost.

Uses only existing LoadBalancer hooks (SelectServer/Feedback,
need_feedback) with DoublyBufferedData membership like rr/la; per-node
stats are shared_ptr-owned by both buffers. Registered as "p2c" in
global.cpp. Includes unit tests (functional, weighted, exclusion,
error punishment, concurrency churn) and docs in cn/en client.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Reuse SelectIn.begin_time_us to avoid extra clock read per selection

Fix inline redis protocol consuming HTTP/2 connection preface (#3338)

Inline redis protocol support (#3024) accepts any alpha-leading line as
an inline command. The HTTP/2 client connection preface
("PRI * HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n") is alpha-leading, so it was parsed
as an inline command instead of returning PARSE_ERROR_TRY_OTHERS. This
prevented protocol auto-detection from falling through to HTTP/2, and
gRPC clients calling a server with redis_service enabled failed with
"connection closed before server preface received".

Detect the HTTP/2 preface (fully, or as a not-yet-complete prefix) in
the inline branch of RedisCommandParser::ConsumeImpl and defer to other
protocols. A command-name blacklist is not viable because some HTTP
methods are also valid redis commands (e.g. GET), whereas the preface
is a fixed magic string that no redis command begins with, making the
check unambiguous.

optimize crc32c for riscv64 with Zbc carry-less multiplication (#3312)

* optimize crc32c for riscv64 with Zbc carry-less multiplication

Implement hardware-accelerated CRC32C for RISC-V using the Zbc
(carry-less multiplication) extension. The implementation uses
128-bit folding with 4-way parallelism and Barrett reduction,
following the approach from Hadoop PR #8371.

Key changes:
- Add rv_clmul/rv_clmulh inline assembly wrappers
- Implement 128-bit fold with 4-way parallel processing (64 bytes/iter)
- Add Barrett reduction for final 128-bit to 32-bit conversion
- Runtime CPU feature detection via /proc/cpuinfo
- Compile-time guard: #ifdef __riscv_zbc
- CMake option: WITH_RISCV_ZBC (default OFF)

Performance: 3-4x speedup over table-based 8-byte unrolled baseline,
~1.1 GB/s throughput on 1MB data.
Correctness: Verified against RFC 3720 B.4 and bitwise reference.

Signed-off-by: Felix-Gong <gongxiaofei24@iscas.ac.cn>

* fix: wrap isSSE42() in #ifdef __SSE4_2__ to fix -Wunused-function

feat(auto_cl): add error rate threshold for punishment attenuation (#3219)

* feat(auto_cl): add error rate threshold for punishment attenuation

Add new GFlag `auto_cl_error_rate_punish_threshold` to enable
error-rate-based punishment attenuation in AutoConcurrencyLimiter.

Problem: Low error rates (e.g., 1.3% sporadic timeouts) cause
disproportionate avg_latency inflation (+31%), leading the limiter
to mistakenly shrink max_concurrency and trigger ELIMIT rejections.

Solution: Inspired by Alibaba Sentinel's threshold-based approach:
- threshold=0 (default): Original behavior preserved (backward compat)
- threshold>0 (e.g., 0.1): Error rates below threshold produce zero
  punishment; above it, punishment scales linearly from 0 to full

Example: With threshold=0.1, a 5% error rate produces no punishment,
while a 50% error rate produces 44% of the original punishment.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add new GFlag `auto_cl_error_rate_punish_threshold` to enable
error-rate-based punishment attenuation in AutoConcurrencyLimiter.

Problem: Low error rates (e.g., 1.3% sporadic timeouts) cause
disproportionate avg_latency inflation (+31%), leading the limiter
to mistakenly shrink max_concurrency and trigger ELIMIT rejections.

Solution: Inspired by Alibaba Sentinel's threshold-based approach:
- threshold=0 (default): Original behavior preserved (backward compat)
- threshold>0 (e.g., 0.1): Error rates below threshold produce zero
  punishment; above it, punishment scales linearly from 0 to full

Example: With threshold=0.1, a 5% error rate produces no punishment,
while a 50% error rate produces 44% of the original punishment.

from the parsed byte; also limit flexible-mode reference chain to at
most three references.

`hasGof`) with bounds checks and c

fix: limit AMF decoder nesting depth (#4787)

### Motivation
- Prevent unbounded recursive-descent parsing in the AMF decoder that
allowed deeply nested AMF objects/arrays to exhaust the process stack
and cause a pre-auth remote DoS.

### Description
- Add an RAII depth guard `AMFDecoder::DepthGuard` and a per-decoder
`depth` counter with `kMaxDepth = 64` to `AMFDecoder` in
`src/Rtmp/amf.h`/`src/Rtmp/amf.cpp`.
- Instrument `load_object()`, `load_ecma()`, and `load_arr()` to create
a `DepthGuard` at entry so nesting is incremented and reliably
decremented on return or exception, and throw
`std::runtime_error("Maximum AMF nesting depth exceeded")` when the
limit is exceeded.
- Add `tests/test_amf.cpp` to assert that a 64-level nested AMF
container is accepted and a 65-level nested container is rejected with
the expected error.
- Keep non-nested parsing behavior unchanged; the guard only enforces a
maximum container nesting depth.

### Testing
- Configured the project with tests enabled u

by certain servers actively closing the connection.

feat(matter): allow setting Matter Descriptor TagList attribute for endpoint (#12776)

* feat(matter): allow setting Descriptor TagList on Generic Switch endpoints

Adds MatterGenericSwitch::setTagList() so sketches can tag sibling
Generic Switch endpoints (e.g. multiple smart buttons) with standard
Matter semantic tags, letting controllers disambiguate them instead of
relying on endpoint order alone.

Adds the MatterSmartButtonsTagList example, demonstrating two tagged
buttons (On/Off).

Closes #11515

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(matter): use esp_matter::endpoint::set_semantic_tags for TagList

The prebuilt Matter static library linked by this repo's Arduino build
does not export connectedhomeip's raw SetTagList() free function
(undefined reference at link time), even though it declares it in
attribute-storage.h. Switch to esp_matter's own
endpoint::set_semantic_tags() wrapper, which is actually exported by
libespressif__esp_matter.a and is a thinner

feat(zigbee): Allow ZigbeeEP implementers to handle raw ZCL commands (#12479)

* feat(zigbee): Add raw command handler for ZigbeeEP

Register a raw ZCL command handler via esp_zb_raw_command_handler_register()
that forwards all incoming ZCL commands to endpoint implementations before
the ZBOSS stack processes them.

This allows ZigbeeEP subclasses to observe and optionally consume cluster-
specific commands (e.g., On/Off, Level Control, Off with effect) that were
previously handled only internally by the stack. By default, the handler
returns false so the stack continues normal processing — existing behavior
is fully preserved.

New API:
- zb_raw_command_t struct with cluster_id, command_id, data, etc.
- ZigbeeEP::zbRawCommand() virtual method for subclass override
- ZigbeeEP::onRawCommand() callback registration for user sketches

Closes https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/issues/12025

GH-45086: [C++] Fix heap buffer overflow in FillNullForward/Backward … (#50843)

### Rationale for this change

Fixes issue #45086 by fixing a heap heap buffer overflow in
FillNullForward/Backward on chunked boolean arrays.

### What changes are included in this PR?

FillNullForwardChunked and FillNullBackwardChunked sized each output
chunk's data buffer as `type->byte_width() * chunk->length()`. For
BooleanType, byte_width() returns 0 (bit_width() / 8, truncated by
integer division), so the buffer was allocated with 0 bytes while the
chunk's declared length was unchanged, and filling it wrote real bit
data past the end of the allocation.

~~Add DataType::bytes_required(num_elements), a virtual method alongside
byte_width()/bit_width() that correctly rounds up for bit-packed types,
and use it at both call sites instead of the byte_width()-based
calculation. Add regression tests exercising fill-null-forward and
fill-null-backward on a chunked boolean array with a chunk large enough
to r

### Rationale for this change

IPC schema serialization already treats extension arrays as their storage type. Record batch serialization still handled extension arrays according to the logical `extension` type when deciding whether to emit a validity buffer. - teach `RecordBatchSerializer::VisitArray()` to use the physical storage array when deciding common IPC buffer handling for extension arrays
- keep field-node accounting on the logical extension array while delegating layout-sensitive buffer decisions to the storage array

### Rationale for this change

Fixes #50481. `arrow::csv::TableReader`/`BlockParser` can silently mis-split a row when a text field contains an embedded NUL (`0x00`) byte, once the reader has processed enough data to switch into its SIMD "bulk filter" scanning path.

### What changes are included in this PR?

`SSE42Filter::Matches` (`cpp/src/arrow/csv/lexing_internal.h`) uses `_mm_cmpistrc`, an **implicit-length** SSE4.2 string-compare intrinsic that treats `0x00` as a terminator in both operands. Since the caller feeds it 8 raw CSV bytes at a time, a real quote/comma/newline sharing an 8-byte word with an embedded NUL becomes invisible to the filter — `RunBulkFilter` then trusts the filter's "no special chars" answer and bulk-copies the whole word, silently swallowing the structural character.

An initial version of this fix switched to the explicit-length `_mm_cmpestrc`, passing the true length of eac

### Rationale for this change

Attempting downcasting on UINT64  Fields when converting them from Arrow to R works fine on individual arrays, but fails on list arrays, because we only use the individual row to work out whether to downcast.

I considered a few different solutions but I concluded that this one is the least complex while presenting a good solution -  having UINT64  always be converted to doubles and never attempt downcasting.  

The impact here is that people who are expecting integers via downcasting will see a change in behaviour, but I think there's a strong argument here that if you are using UINT64  to store values that can be downcast, you probably need to be using UINT32 anyway.

GH-50182: [C++][Parquet] Fix truncated min/max statistics for all-infinity floating-point columns (#50183)

### Rationale for this change

When every value in a `FLOAT`, `DOUBLE`, or `FLOAT16` column is the same infinity, the Parquet writer stored a *finite* min/max statistic instead of the infinity actually present in the column:

- all `+Inf` → `min` written as `FLT_MAX` / `DBL_MAX` (should be `+Inf`)
- all `-Inf` → `max` written as `-FLT_MAX` / `-DBL_MAX` (should be `-Inf`)

The running min/max were seeded with `std::numeric_limits<T>::max()` / `::lowest()` — the largest/smallest *finite* values. These are not identity elements for min/max once the data contains infinities: `Min(FLT_MAX, +Inf)` keeps `FLT_MAX`, so an all-`+Inf` column never displaces the seed (and symmetrically for `-Inf`). The wrong value is then written with `is_min_value_exact = true`, so a reader is told the exact minimum of an all-`+Inf` column is `FLT_MAX` — a value not even present in the column. Range-based

Report .eh_frame relocations that do not fit in 32 bits

FDEs refer to their functions with 32-bit PC-relative relocations, and
.eh_frame_hdr stores 32-bit offsets, but mold applied them without any
range check. A function more than 2 GiB away from .eh_frame, which
happens with a huge text section or with -Ttext or --section-start
placing code far from the default layout, silently got a wrapped-around
FDE that the unwinder cannot use, while GNU ld and lld reject such
links. Those relocations are now range-checked like all others, and so
are the .eh_frame_hdr entries.

The aarch64 long thunk test placed code with unwind tables 4 GiB away
from .eh_frame and relied on the bogus FDEs going unnoticed. It now
compiles the far functions without unwind tables and keeps the far
section fixed while swapping the functions between the sections, so
calls in both directions are still covered.

FDEs refer to their functions with 32-bit PC-relative relocations, and
.eh_frame_hdr stores 32-bit offsets, but mold applied them without any
range check. A function more than 2 GiB away from .eh_frame, which
happens with a huge text section or with -Ttext or --section-start
placing code far from the default layout, silently got a wrapped-around

links. Those relocations are now range-checked like all others, and so
are the .eh_frame_hdr entries.

from .eh_frame and relied on the bogus FDEs going unnoticed. It now
compiles the far functions without unwind tables and keeps the far
section fixed while swapping the functions between the sections, so
calls in both directions are still covered.

Match quoted names in version scripts and dynamic lists literally

GNU ld takes a quoted name in a version script or a dynamic list as a
literal string, while an unquoted one is a glob pattern. mold dropped
the quotes and treated everything as a pattern, so `"operator
delete[](void*)"` in an `extern "C++"` block never matched anything
because `[]` parsed as an empty character class. Glob metacharacters in
a quoted name are now escaped before the name is handed to the matcher.

Count section piece symbols while parsing sections

reattach_section_pieces() traversed every relocation of every alloc
section once just to count the references to mergeable sections, so
that it could allocate their symbols at once, and then traversed them
again to create the symbols. The count needs only ELF data, so it is
now taken while the sections are parsed, where a CREL relocation table

When a symbol with hidden visibility resolved to a DSO, symbol
resolution started over from scratch for all symbols with that DSO
definition excluded, and Chromium has three such symbols. Resolution is
independent per symbol, so only those symbols are resolved again, and
if one of them moves to an archive member that is not reachable yet,

The job that read a thin archive opened all of its members before
feeding them to the reader loop, so a large archive's members were

Support DWARF 5 type units in gdb index

With -gdwarf-5 -fdebug-types-section, GCC moves each type into its own
type unit and emits it as a one-section COMDAT .debug_info contribution,
so an object file contains several .debug_info sections. We assumed one
.debug_info section per file containing nothing but compilation units:
type units were missing from the index, and a pubnames offset could be
interpreted relative to the wrong contribution.

Read every live .debug_info contribution instead, classifying units by
their header's unit_type. Type units are collected into the .gdb_index
type-unit table along with their signatures, and each pubnames set is
matched to its contribution through the relocation on the set header's
debug_info_offset field. COMDAT group selection has already discarded
duplicate type units by the time we read them, so exactly one copy of
each type unit is indexed.

Fix spurious duplicate symbol error with mixed LTO and non-LTO archives

If an IR file claims a COMDAT group, the LTO result provides the group's
contents. However, post-LTO COMDAT group selection started from a clean
slate, so an archive member extracted only after LTO could win a claimed
group, resurrecting a copy that collides with the LTO result.

Remember the claim on the signature symbol, and let only LTO-generated
files win such a group after LTO. LLVM keeps claimed groups in its
output; GCC emits their contents without a group, so no file wins.

Fixes https://github.com/rui314/mold/issues/1637

Report duplicate definitions of a versioned symbol

A default-versioned symbol `foo@@VER` can be referred to not only as
`foo` but also as `foo@VER`, so defining both `foo@@VER` and `foo@VER`
is a duplicate definition of the versioned name. We didn't diagnose it
and silently emitted a dynamic symbol table containing two definitions
of `foo@VER`, leaving it up to the dynamic loader which one a versioned
reference binds to. GNU ld and lld reject this; now we do too.

We check for duplicates by scanning the dynamic symbol table once it's
populated, because the problem manifests if and only if both symbols
are exported, and the exported set is much smaller than the set of all
symbols. GNU ld additionally reports the error for non-exported
symbols; lld doesn't, and we behave like lld.

Fixes https://github.com/rui314/mold/issues/828

Intern symbols without a concurrent hash table

Like the previous commit did for comdat groups, symbol interning no
longer goes through a single concurrent hash table. Object file
parsing only records each global symbol name along with which slot of
the file's symbol vector it belongs to; gather_symbols() then

Previously, data appended to the output file, such as .gdb_index,

.gdb_index was constructed in a malloc'ed buffer that close()

Compute ICF digests from the previous round's digests

A propagation round used to compute a vertex's next digest by hashing
its initial digest together with its neighbors' current digests,
which required keeping three digest arrays: the initial one and two
that alternate between current and next.

Hash the vertex's current digest instead of its initial one. This is
the textbook formulation of iterated partition refinement, and it
distinguishes exactly the same vertex pairs in every round: a current
digest determines the initial digest injectively (up to hash
collisions, which the whole algorithm already assumes away), so the
per-round partitions, the number of rounds and the final equivalence
classes are all unchanged.

The initial digest array disappears, saving 16 bytes per vertex, and
the current/next arrays are now two plainly named vectors that swap
after each round instead of an indexed triple with a flip-flop slot
index.

Merge ICF leaf sections by digest

Leaf sections used to be merged with a dedicated hash map keyed by
raw section contents, with its own hasher and equality functor. That
equality was subtly weaker than the one the propagation rounds use:
it compared FDE bodies but ignored which CIE each FDE points to, so
two identical functions whose CIEs recorded different personality
routines could be merged incorrectly. It also ignored section flags.

Instead, compute the same digest for leaves that compute_digest
produces for graph sections and merge leaves through DigestMap, the
same structure the propagation rounds use. One definition of section
equality now covers both paths, which fixes the personality bug, and
LeafHasher, LeafEq and the last digest-keyed use of tbb's hash map in
this file disappear.

The trade-off is that leaf merging now relies on 128-bit digest
uniqueness instead of comparing contents exactly, but that is the
same assumption the rest of ICF is already built on.

Count distinct ICF digests on every propagation round

To detect convergence of the ICF propagation rounds, we count the
number of distinct digests and stop when it ceases to increase. We
previously gated the count on a cheaper necessary-looking condition:
as long as the number of changed digests per round was still moving,

partition, because sections in the same equivalence class change

are all distinct from the start, the partition is final after the
first round, but the changed-digest count keeps moving until the
propagation depth reaches the chain length, so the gate would delay
termination by the depth of the chain.

stop as soon as the count repeats, which is the earliest round at

Make --emit-relocs reflect relaxed instructions on RISC-V and LoongArch

After relaxation, the relocations attached to the relaxed instructions no
longer match the new, shorter instructions. With --emit-relocs we copied the
input relocations verbatim, emitting stale types at stale offsets.

Rewrite each relocation's offset and type in RelocSection::copy_buf to match
the relaxed code, recomputing the outcome the same way apply_reloc_alloc
recomputes its instruction rewrites. -r output is not relaxed, so its
relocations are passed through unchanged.

Fixes https://github.com/rui314/mold/issues/1584

Use .gnu.version_r when registering undefined DSO symbols

For an undefined symbol in a shared library, mold treated the versym
as VER_NDX_GLOBAL and registered the symbol under its bare name. That
meant an undef foo@VER_1.0 in libbar.so was looked up as just foo, so
a non-default foo@VER_1.0 in another DSO did not satisfy it and
--no-allow-shlib-undefined wrongly reported "undefined symbol: foo".

Parse .gnu.version_r and, when an undef has a versym indexing into it,
register the symbol as name@VERSION so the existing versioned-symbol
resolution path picks up matching definitions.

Fixes https://github.com/rui314/mold/issues/1571

Don't unconditionally retain C-identifier-named sections in --gc-sections

A section whose name is a valid C identifier was treated as a GC root,
keeping it (and everything reachable from it) alive even when nothing
referenced its synthesized __start_/__stop_ marker symbols. That could
pull in unrelated code with undefined references and cause spurious
"undefined symbol" errors that lld and ld.bfd don't produce.

Build a multimap of c-identifier-named sections up front and, during
marking, when a relocation targets __start_<name> or __stop_<name>,
mark every section named <name> alive.

Fixes https://github.com/rui314/mold/issues/1571

Add --pack-dyn-relocs=android support

Implements the Android Packed Relocations Format (APS2) used by Android
binaries to compress dynamic relocations. Two new modes are accepted:
`--pack-dyn-relocs=android` encodes all dynamic relocations as APS2 in
.rela.dyn (SHT_ANDROID_RELA) and emits DT_ANDROID_RELA(SZ) instead of
DT_RELA(SZ); `--pack-dyn-relocs=android+relr` is the same but with
R_RELATIVE relocations diverted to .relr.dyn via the existing RELR path.

The encoder groups consecutive relocations sharing offset_delta and
r_info to amortize SLEB128 overhead. The encoded bytes are decoded by
Android's bionic loader and by llvm-readelf, which the new test uses to
verify correctness.

main.cc gains a final set_osec_offsets() call after fix_synthetic_symbols.
Symbol values assigned there change addends for relocations that
reference synthetic symbols, which can shift the SLEB128-encoded section
size; re-running the layout convergence keeps sh_size consistent with
the final encoding.

Centralize dynamic relocation generation in RelDynSection

Previously each chunk wrote its dynamic relocations into a magic offset
in .rel.dyn (tracked via per-chunk reldyn_offset), with a separate
construct_relr pass building per-chunk relr vectors. Now each chunk
returns its dynrels via a virtual collect_dynrels(), and RelDynSection
aggregates them into a single relocs vector that it owns and writes.
RELR-eligibility is determined by checking r_offset alignment of the
collected ElfRel entries (replacing the ABS_REL_RELR kind).

* Fix #2435: allow mmap to open files held open for writing

Add FILE_SHARE_WRITE to the share mode passed to ::CreateFile2 so
detail::mmap can open a file even when another process holds it open
with GENERIC_WRITE (e.g. an active log file). Without this, CreateFile2
fails with ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION because the new opener's share mode
must permit the existing handle's access mode.

This brings the Windows path's behavior in line with the POSIX path
which uses ::open(O_RDONLY) and is unaffected by other processes'
write handles.

Reproducer test for #2431 (getaddrinfo_a use-after-free) (#2433)

* Add reproducer for #2431 (getaddrinfo_a use-after-free)

On Linux/glibc, getaddrinfo_with_timeout() runs DNS asynchronously via
getaddrinfo_a(GAI_NOWAIT) using a stack-local gaicb. When gai_suspend()
hits the connection timeout, gai_cancel() is called and the function
returns immediately — but gai_cancel() is non-blocking and can return
EAI_NOTCANCELED, leaving the resolver worker thread alive and still
referencing the destroyed stack frame.

Adds three opt-in gtest cases (GetAddrInfoAsyncCancelTest.*) that
exercise the cancel path repeatedly. They are gated on Linux/glibc +
CPPHTTPLIB_USE_NON_BLOCKING_GETADDRINFO at compile time, and on the
CPPHTTPLIB_TEST_ISSUE_2431=1 env var at runtime, so a normal `make
test` run is unaffected.

Also adds a dedicated CI job (issue-2431-repro) and a Docker-based
local runner (test/run_issue_2431_repro.sh) that sinkhole UDP/53 so
the timeout branch is taken, and run the test under AS

fix(config): accept an endpoint in a legacy client block and validate the port

Four defects found in review, each confirmed against the real agent binary before
being changed.

The MSI reconfigures a preserved 4.x ossec.conf in place. With no <agent> block
to target it writes the endpoint into <client><server>, and
Read_Legacy_Client_Address() skipped every child that was not <address> -- so an
upgraded agent had no manager at all and refused to start with
"(4105): No valid server IP found." That block now reads <endpoint> too, through
the same parser, so a port and prefix written there survive.

The port was not range-checked. "curl has already range-checked this" was simply
untrue: <endpoint>10.0.0.5:0</endpoint> was accepted and yielded port 0, while
every installer parser rejects anything below 1.

A trailing ':' is "no port" to curl, so <endpoint>10.0.0.5:</endpoint> was
accepted and silently fell back to 1517 -- a value the installers reject, and
that test_register_configure_age

fix(agent): do not remove a who-data socket the agent cannot recreate

Review feedback on the probe.

The stale-socket cleanup was not guarded by restart_audit. With
<restart_audit>no</restart_audit> the agent cannot restart Auditd to recreate
the socket, so three transient connection failures turned a single failed start
into who-data being broken on every start from then on. The socket is now only
removed when Auditd can be restarted to bring it back.

The connect that follows wait_for_audit_socket() was single-shot, which
contradicts the reason audit_socket_connect_retry() exists: one transient
refusal was enough to discard a candidate that works and settle on a different
template, or to report (6636) on the last one. It retries there too.

The fallback debug message assumed the previous candidate had been applied and
produced no socket, which is not true when it could not be written or Auditd
refused to restart with it -- a path the tests exercise. Those two cases now say
so instea

fix(agent): decide the audisp configuration from a live socket, not from the file on disk

Review feedback on the probing logic. Preferring whatever configuration was
already on disk deduced "what works" from the contents of a file, which is a
weak signal: after a probe that failed on every candidate, the file holds the
last and least preferred one, so a host that later becomes viable -- say
audispd-plugins gets installed on audit >= 4.0.3 -- would latch onto the wrong
template, and "the socket exists and accepts connections" cannot detect a wrong
event format.

The strong signal is a socket that is up and can be connected to. When there is
one, the agent now keeps it untouched if the configuration behind it is one this
agent could have written, and rewrites the file otherwise; the candidate list is
always walked in version order, so logging (6054) on anything past the first
candidate means again exactly what it says.

fix(agent): probe the audisp configuration instead of trusting the audit version

FIM who-data never started on Amazon Linux 2023 agents using the audit
provider. Audit 3.1.5 is bucketed into the plugin configuration that
renders a three token args line, but Amazon's 3.1.5 rebuild ships an
audisp-af_unix that only accepts two: it logged "Missing arguments, using
defaults", bound its own default socket, and init_auditd_socket() had
nothing to connect to, so the agent reported (6636) and fell back to
real-time for the life of the process.

The audit version cannot tell a vendor rebuild apart from the upstream
release it is based on -- the very same three token line works on
AlmaLinux 9's audit 3.1.5 -- so the version is no longer taken as proof.
The configuration expected for the installed version is still applied
first, but the agent now waits for the socket to appear and checks that it
can connect before accepting it, and probes the remaining known
configuration when it cannot, reporti

[CPU:Feature] Optimize LinearAttention with NEON assembly and fp16 support

Optimize gated_delta_rule recurrence with dedicated CoreFunctions kernels:
- MNNDualMatVec: fused dual MatVec (S^T@k, S^T@q) replacing two separate loops
- MNNDecayRankOneUpdate: fused decay + rank-1 update (S = decay*S + k⊗delta)
- MNNRankOneUpdate: rank-1 update for non-decay path
- ARM64 NEON assembly with 16-wide main loop + 4/1 tail handling

Full fp16 pipeline on Arm82 backend:
- Add LinearAttention to opCompabilityForLowp whitelist
- All tensors/state in fp16, bytes-aware buffer allocation via int8_t
- 3 new fp16 NEON assembly kernels (MNNRankOneUpdateFp16.S)
- Conv1D+SiLu: fp16→fp32 bulk convert, vectorized MNNSiLu, fp32→fp16 back
- Decay (exp) kept in fp32 (MNNExp requirement), scalar per timestep

Performance (Mac M-series, 4 threads, H=16 dk=dv=64):
- fp32 vs baseline: prefill ~20-34% faster, decode ~4-13% faster
- fp16 vs fp32: prefill ~19-51% faster, decode ~28-45% faster

AP_HAL_SITL: add --sim-periph-lockstep option

Simulated peripherals are clock slaves: they set their simulated time
from the vehicle's multicast state packets, and the vehicle never
waits for them.  On a loaded machine a peripheral starved of
wall-clock time falls behind in simulation time by the starvation
multiplied by the speedup, so its data streams (DroneCAN GPS fixes,
for example) develop simulation-time gaps large enough to trip
consumers' health monitoring.  This is why supplementary-binary tests
have been restricted to speedup 1.

With --sim-periph-lockstep the vehicle does not advance the
simulation past a state packet until every registered peripheral has
acknowledged consuming it.  Peripherals register on their first
reply (the reply now carries a timestamp echo alongside the existing
servo feedback); a peripheral that stops replying for a wall-clock
second is presumed dead - the test harness terminates them without
notice - and is evicted with a warning, re-registering on

Plane: gradual RTL altitude descent in QRTL approach

Previously, once QRTL's approach phase started, the target altitude
snapped straight to RTL_ALTITUDE regardless of how much higher the
vehicle actually was, causing an immediate steep descent while still
far from home. The target now ramps down gradually from the vehicle's
actual altitude at the start of the approach to RTL_ALTITUDE, reaching
it at the same distance-from-home threshold where the existing
RTL_ALTITUDE -> Q_RTL_ALT approach ramp already begins, so the two
ramps join continuously. If the vehicle is at or below RTL_ALTITUDE at
that point, behaviour is unchanged.

The altitude and distance at the start of the approach are latched in
ModeQRTL rather than taken from the fixed wing waypoint altitude
offset, which is cleared as the destination is neared. As for fixed
wing waypoints, ALT_SLOPE_MIN gates the ramp: setting it to zero
disables the gradual descent, and altitude changes smaller than it are
still made immediately;

mutation_compactor: count partitions continued from the previous page

compaction_stats::dead_partitions() is computed as
total_partitions - live_partitions, on uint64_t. total_partitions is only
incremented by consume_new_partition(), which is driven by a partition-start
fragment from the reader, while live_partitions is incremented by
partition_is_not_empty(), on the first fragment emitted from the partition.

A page which continues a partition started on a previous page resumes the
reader mid-partition, so it never sees a partition-start fragment. The
partition is therefore not counted in total_partitions, while emitting rows
still counts it in live_partitions, and dead_partitions() underflows. This
is visible in the page stats trace, e.g.:

    Page stats: 0 partition(s) (1 live, 18446744073709551615 dead), ...,
    100 clustering row(s) (100 live, 0 dead), ...

Account for such partitions in start_new_page(), based on the region of the
peeked next fragment, which is already passed

sstables_loader: Support 'prefix' in tablet-aware-restore API

The tablet_aware_restore handler used to reject any request with a
non-empty backup_location 'prefix', always assuming manifest entries
were absolute object keys under the bucket root.

Thread 'prefix' from restore_tablets() into
populate_snapshot_sstables_from_manifests(), joining it with each
manifest entry the same way start_restore already does, so manifests
are resolved relative to the backup location's prefix.

Fix download_tablet_sstables() to actually combine
snapshot_remote_locations.prefix with each row's own
snapshot_sstables.prefix instead of silently discarding the former,
closing the last gap that made a non-empty prefix unusable end to end.

When a storage group enters split mode it creates two compaction groups, one per
side of the split point, and routes writes to them by token. Each of them was
created with make_empty_group(), which copies the range of the group being split,
so both were told they span the whole tablet range while neither can ever hold more
than half of it.

That misleads the sstable set. partitioned_sstable_set stores an sstable in a flat
vector, rather than in its interval map, only when the sstable spans at least 85% of
the range the set was given; the vector exists precisely to keep sstables which
overlap everything out of a structure whose size is the number of (sub-range,
sstable) incidences. An sstable flushed by a split-ready group covers at most its
own side of the split point, so against the whole tablet range it measures about
50%, misses the threshold, and lands in the interval map together with every other

compaction: register backlog tracker of compaction groups created after start

replica::compaction_group's constructor builds its backlog tracker but never
registers it with compaction_backlog_manager. The only registration path is
table::set_compaction_strategy(), which runs at table start and on schema
change, so it only ever covers the compaction groups that exist at that
moment.

Groups created later -- by tablet split, tablet migration or tablet merge --
keep a live, correctly charged tracker that nothing ever reads. Their
sstables don't contribute to compaction_manager::backlog(), so the compaction
controller under-provisions shares and scylla_compaction_manager_backlog
under-reports. It decays over time: when a tablet splits or migrates, the old
registered group is destroyed and deregisters its tracker, while the group
that replaces it is unregistered, so after enough tablet churn a shard
reports a zero backlog no matter how many sstables it holds. A schema change
masks it tempo

fix: nullable scalar field filter leaks null documents without inverted index (#410)

When a nullable scalar field has no inverted index, the forward filter path
fails to handle null values from Arrow's filter evaluation:

1. get_forward_bit(): BooleanArray::operator[] returns nullopt for null entries,
   which is_filtered() treats as "no filter" (not filtered), letting null docs
   through. Fix: use value_or(false) to treat null as "not matched".

2. is_matched_by_forward_filter(): reads BooleanScalar.value without checking
   is_valid, which is UB for null scalars. Fix: check is_valid first.

Closes #409

fix(GUI): honor "Ignore" when layer height exceeds the configured maximum (#14369)

* fix(GUI): honor "Ignore" when layer height exceeds the configured maximum

Entering a layer height above the printer's max_layer_height on the Print
Settings tab fired two guards in sequence. Tab::on_value_change prompts
"...Adjust to the set range automatically?" with an Adjust/Ignore choice, and
ConfigManipulation::update_print_fff_config then showed an OK-only "Too large
layer height. Reset to X" dialog whose result was never checked, so it always
reset the value. The second guard overrode the user's "Ignore", resetting the
layer height regardless.

Changes:
- Extract the shared Adjust/Ignore dialog into
  ConfigManipulation::layer_height_out_of_range_dialog, reused by the tab
  (Tab::on_value_change) and the per-object/part settings panels. The dialog now
  names the value it will clamp to and reads correctly for too-low as well as
  too-high.
- The tab/plate path is already covered by Tab::on_val

[map] Fix crash on tap of a temporary relation track selection mark

TrackSelectionInfo::IsRelation() answers "is there relation metadata to
(re)build the temporary track", but BuildTrackPlacePage used it to answer
"is this selection the temporary relation track". A selection restored from
a TrackSelectionMark keeps the track id only, so a tap on the mark of the
currently shown relation track took the ordinary branch, cleared the very
track it was about to fetch and dereferenced a null Track.

Key the decision on the track id instead, so such a tap reuses the already
built track, and null check GetTrack() before use: a selection mark could
also outlive its track, which is what ClearTempRelationTrack() left behind
before 9be7f77d57.

A null check alone would turn the segfault into an abort, because
FillUserMarkInfo ignored the failure and ActivateMapSelection rejects an
OBJECT_EMPTY selection. Propagate it instead, so a stale mark falls back to
the regular tap matching.

- Verify the Skity path with a fixed Roboto fixture that distinguishes real metrics from the legacy heuristic.

Squashed commit of the following:
commit e752f50195445fe647286de3795b10026055401b
Author: naughtyGitCat <psyduck007@outlook.com>
Date:   Sat Jun 6 11:46:25 2026 +0800

    Add graphics adapter (GPU) selection

    Add a "Graphics Adapter" submenu under Settings to choose which physical GPU
    Shotcut renders, decodes, and encodes with. On systems where a low-power
    integrated GPU drives the display while a more capable discrete GPU is also
    present (e.g. an NVIDIA card with no monitor attached), this lets the user direct
    preview rendering, hardware decoding and hardware export to the discrete GPU.

    - gpuinfo.{h,cpp} (new): enumerate physical adapters via DXGI, de-duplicating
      the same GPU that some drivers report multiple times; resolve a GPU's live
      DXGI adapter index from its stable vendor+device id (the raw index is not
      stable across runs on some systems); and pick the hardware encoder family
      matching the sel

{
    if (stage == VertexStage) {
        m_vert = "struct VSInput {"
                 "  float2 vertex : VERTEX;"
                 "  float2 coords : TEXCOORD;"
                 "};"
                 "struct VSOutput {"
                 "  float2 coords : TEXCOORD0;"
                 "  float4 position : SV_Position;"
                 "};"
                 "VSOutput main(VSInput input) {"
                 "  VSOutput output;"
                 "  output.position = float4(input.vertex, 0.0f, 1.0f);"
                 "  output.coords = input.coords;"
                 "  return output;"
                 "}";
        Q_ASSERT(!m_vert.isEmpty());
        m_vertEntryPoint = QByteArrayLiteral("main");
    } else {
        m_frag = "Texture2D yTex, uTex, vTex;"
                 "SamplerState yuvSampler;"
                 "cbuffer buf {"
                 "    int colorspace;"
                 "};"
                 "struct PSInput {"
                 "  float2 coords : TEXCOORD0;"
                 "};"
                 "struct PSOutput {"
                 "  float4 color : SV_Target0;"
                 "};"
                 "PSOutput main(PSInput input) {"
                 "  float3 yuv;"
                 "  yuv.x = yTex.Sample(yuvSampler, input.coords).r -  16.0f/255.0f;"
                 "  yuv.y = uTex.Sample(yuvSampler, input.coords).r - 128.0f/255.0f;"
                 "  yuv.z = vTex.Sample(yuvSampler, input.coords).r - 128.0f/255.0f;"
                 "  float3x3 coefficients;"
                 "  if (colorspace == 601) {"
                 "    coefficients = float3x3("
                 "      1.1643f,  0.0f,      1.5958f,"
                 "      1.1643f, -0.39173f, -0.8129f,"
                 "      1.1643f,  2.017f,    0.0f);"
                 "  } else if (colorspace == 2020) {" // ITU-R BT.2020
                 "    coefficients = float3x3("
                 "      1.1643f,  0.0f,    1.7167f,"
                 "      1.1643f, -0.1873f, -0.6504f,"
                 "      1.1643f,  2.1418f,  0.0f);"
                 "  } else {" // ITU-R 709
                 "    coefficients = float3x3("
                 "      1.1643f,  0.0f,    1.793f,"
                 "      1.1643f, -0.213f, -0.533f,"
                 "      1.1643f,  2.112f,  0.0f);"
                 "  }"
                 "  PSOutput output;"
                 "  output.color = float4(mul(coefficients, yuv), 1.0f);"
                 "  return output;"

void OpenGLVideoWidget::createShader()
{
    m_shader.reset(new QOpenGLShaderProgram);
    m_shader->addShaderFromSourceCode(QOpenGLShader::Vertex,
                                      "uniform highp mat4 projection;"
                                      "uniform highp mat4 modelView;"
                                      "attribute highp vec4 vertex;"
                                      "attribute highp vec2 texCoord;"
                                      "varying highp vec2 coordinates;"
                                      "void main(void) {"
                                      "  gl_Position = projection * modelView * vertex;"
                                      "  coordinates = texCoord;"
                                      "}");
    m_shader
        ->addShaderFromSourceCode(QOpenGLShader::Fragment,
                                  "uniform sampler2D Ytex, Utex, Vtex;"
                                  "uniform lowp int colorspace;"
                                  "varying highp vec2 coordinates;"
                                  "void main(void) {"
                                  "  mediump vec3 texel;"
                                  "  texel.r = texture2D(Ytex, coordinates).r -  16.0/255.0;" // Y
                                  "  texel.g = texture2D(Utex, coordinates).r - 128.0/255.0;" // U
                                  "  texel.b = texture2D(Vtex, coordinates).r - 128.0/255.0;" // V
                                  "  mediump mat3 coefficients;"
                                  "  if (colorspace == 601) {"
                                  "    coefficients = mat3("
                                  "      1.1643,  1.1643,  1.1643,"    // column 1
                                  "      0.0,    -0.39173, 2.017,"     // column 2
                                  "      1.5958, -0.8129,  0.0);"      // column 3
                                  "  } else if (colorspace == 2020) {" // ITU-R BT.2020
                                  "    coefficients = mat3("
                                  "      1.1643, 1.1643, 1.1643," // column 1
                                  "      0.0,   -0.1873, 2.1418," // column 2
                                  "      1.7167, -0.6504, 0.0);"  // column 3
                                  "  } else {"                    // ITU-R 709
                                  "    coefficients = mat3("
                                  "      1.1643, 1.1643, 1.1643," // column 1
                                  "      0.0,   -0.213,  2.112,"  // column 2
                                  "      1.793, -0.533,  0.0);"   // column 3
                                  "  }"
                                  "  gl_FragColor = vec4(coefficients * texel, 1.0);"
                                  "}");
    m_shader->link();
    m_textureLocation[0] = m_shader->uniformLocation("Ytex");
    m_textureLocation[1] = m_shader->uniformLocation("Utex");
    m_textureLocation[2] = m_shader->uniformLocation("Vtex");
    m_colorspaceLocation = m_shader->uniformLocation("colorspace");
    m_projectionLocation = m_shader->uniformLocation("projection");
    m_modelViewLocation = m_shader->uniformLocation("modelView");
    m_vertexLocation = m_shader->attributeLocation("vertex");
    m_texCoordLocation = m_shader->attributeLocation("texCoord");
}

  - This window is not only useful for HDR. Some might like it over the other system display options because fullscreen is optional but also filter overlays are still in the main window.
  - HDR is working for me on macOS and Windows but not yet Linux.
  - Keyboard shortcut <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>`</kbd> opens or *raises* it if already open (convenient for single screen).  
- Move the **External Monitor** sub-menu to the **Player** main menu so it is more convenient.
- Adds **Dynamic range** to the **Add Custom Video Mode** dialog: SDR, HLG HDR, or PQ HDR. Automatic video mo

Engraving: add tests for the ownership and layout parent relations

Pin down the contract the previous commits arrived at: what parent(),
ownershipParent() and layoutParent() each return while an item is merely
constructed, attached and detached again; where the two relations
deliberately diverge (pages, systems and measures are owned by the score
but placed on each other; spanner segments and beams float above them);
what the ownership relation implies for lifetime (a spanner frees its
segments, and a freed segment unplaces itself from its system); and the
invariants that every laid-out item reaches a page through layoutParent(),
and finds its tick and measure through the ownership chain.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Engraving: a beam's system is derived from its elements, not its parent

A beam is drawn on the system of its first chord/rest, so compute
Beam::system() live from the elements instead of caching the system in
the DOM parent slot during layout and resetting it afterwards ("beam
parent does not survive layout"). Beams have no DOM owner - their
lifetime is managed by their ChordRests via removeDeleteBeam() - so
they are now parented to the dummy from the start, which also removes
the need for every file reader to reset the parent of freshly read
beams.

Since a beam no longer has a parent to be removed from, removeChordRest()
drops the generated beam through Score::removeElement() directly, rather
than reaching it through the system (which only forwarded there anyway,
and would have needed a null check now that system() can be null).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Engraving: a spanner frees the segments it owns

Now that a SpannerSegment's owner is its Spanner, the spanner has to delete
its segments. It never did: nothing deletes them when the spanner goes away,
so every deleted spanner (undoing an added hairpin and then dropping the redo
stack, say) left a segment behind, unparented onto the dummy with a dangling
spanner() pointer, until the score itself was destroyed.

eraseSpannerSegments() already does exactly the right cleanup, so call it.
This is only safe because segments now unplace themselves when destroyed:
freeing them here otherwise leaves the systems that placed them holding
pointers to freed memory.

Engraving: separate a system's page placement from its parent

Same treatment as measures: System stores the page it is laid out on in
an explicit m_page field (page()/setPage()) returned via layoutParent(),
instead of overloading the DOM parent slot. Its DOM parent is now the
owning score (Score::m_systems manages system lifetime), attached right
in the constructor, and a setParent(Score*) overload hides
EngravingItem::setParent so that a page can no longer sneak in there.

Since a page's system list and a system's page pointer are maintained
loosely during layout, unlinking is now handled on both ends: ~System
removes itself from its page's list, ~Page clears the page pointer of
the systems it still holds, and the manual detach sites in
Score::removeElement / InsertRemoveMeasures clear the placement
explicitly.

Engraving: separate a measure's system placement from its parent

MeasureBase no longer stores the system it is laid out on in the DOM
parent slot. It gains an explicit m_system placement field (system()/
setSystem()), returned via layoutParent() for the position machinery,
while its DOM parent is now its owner: the score, or the enclosing
frame for nested frames. "Not placed on any system" is now simply
m_system == nullptr rather than a reset explicit-parent flag, and
placing measures during layout no longer thrashes child lists.

MeasureBase/Measure/Box constructors and the corresponding Factory
methods now take the owning Score* instead of a (usually fake dummy)
System*, and the constructor attaches the measure to that score right
away. setParent(Score*) and setParent(Box*) overloads spell out the
two parents a measure can have; they hide EngravingItem::setParent, so
that placement can no longer be reintroduced through the parent slot.

Engraving: walk the layout hierarchy for accessibility

The accessibility tree mirrors what the user sees, so it should follow
the layout parent. It cannot follow it blindly, though: palette items are
parked on the dummy and their accessible parent has to be that dummy, or
the palette loses its accessibility tree altogether. Hence
accessibleParentItem(), which prefers the layout parent and falls back to
the raw parent.

WebSocket: teach the input sink about EOF, and stop losing why a read failed

Follow-up to the previous commit, from Nemoumbra's questions - which found a worse
spin than the one that fix addressed.

InputSink couldn't tell "nothing right now" from "peer is gone": Fill() treats
recv() == 0 as no data and only sets hasError_ on a real error. Block() then waits
with WaitUntilReady(), which reports a closed socket as ready immediately and
forever, so TakeExact() looped on it without ever returning. A client that
disconnects with half a frame buffered - easy to do while blasting messages - put
the server in an infinite loop inside TakeExact, never even returning to Process().
Measured 7.95 CPU-seconds over 8 seconds; 0.08 after.

So: track EOF explicitly (sticky atEnd_, exposed as AtEnd()), and have Block() give
up when nothing more can arrive.

DepthRaster: fix host buffer overflows in the depth raster queue

CalculateDepthDraw guarded depthVertexCount_ with vertexCount, which is the
index count - but depthVertexCount_ grows by the number of decoded vertices,
which for an indexed draw can be far larger. Two draws with 6 indices spanning

at all, which only has room for 3 indices per vertex slot while draws routinely
produce more. Pass the decoded count in separately and check both.

UPnP: fix the exit hang and the CPU spin, and only run the thread when enabled

The two long-standing bug reports had a shared root: the service loop could
end up in a state it never left.

- Exit hang: UPNP_CMD_EXIT was queued alongside port requests and only acted
  on when it reached the front. A request that couldn't complete was never
  popped, so exit sat behind it forever and join() blocked indefinitely.
  Exit is a flag now, checked before anything else.
- CPU spin: wait_for() with a predicate returns immediately when the predicate
  already holds, so a stuck queue head meant a tight loop. sceNetInet's bind()
  queues UPnP_Add regardless of the setting, so this hit whenever UPnP was off
  and a game used sockets. The loop always blocks now, and requests are dropped
  while UPnP is off.
- Failed discovery was retried every 5s forever, each time a full 2s SSDP round
  plus an error toast. Now backs off 5s -> 300s and reports once.

Demangle: rewrite the SN Systems demangler

The old one was reverse engineered from a handful of symbols and got the
shape of the format wrong - it required a digit right after the kind
character, which most real symbols don't have. Measured against a PSP
executable that shipped with its symbol table intact, it decoded 238 of
4662 mangled symbols, most of those incorrectly.

Worked out properly from that binary, the format turns out to be:

  __0 <kind> <name...> <params> [_ <return type>] [<qualifier>]

where the kind character (member function, free function, operator, data)
is the only thing that says how many name components follow, since nothing
separates the last one from the first parameter. Lengths are letters
(A = 0, a = 26); "5" marks an enclosing namespace; "7...._" is a template
argument list, with "4" plus a compact integer for a non-type argument and
"9<index>A" for a back-reference to one; "T<index>" and "N<count><index>"
repeat an earlier parameter; a trailing "K" is co

Demangle: add CodeWarrior and SN Systems symbol demanglers

Older PSP binaries weren't built with GCC, so the Itanium demangler doesn't
help with them. Add two more, tried in turn by DemangleSymbolName():

- Metrowerks CodeWarrior, a descendant of the AT&T cfront scheme
  ("getDistance__6KzUtilFP7st_unitP7st_unit"). Handles Q<n> qualified names,
  the cfront type codes including T/N back-references, cv-qualifiers, and the
  operator/ctor/dtor name codes.
- SN Systems SNC/ProDG ("__0f5DstdIbad_castEwhatvK"), which encodes name
  component lengths as letters. Reverse engineered from a small sample, so
  the parts that are guesses are marked as such - they don't affect the name.

Both are rougher than the Itanium one: they aim for a correctly qualified name
plus a plausible parameter list, and print "..." for a parameter they can't
decode rather than throwing the name away. Results come back as a
DemangledSymbol with the name, parameters, return type and qualifiers kept
separate, in case

Try to not spin so hard in the debugger when stepping

Core_ProcessStepping() returns immediately when the CPU is stopped with nothing
queued, so Core_RunLoopUntil() returns immediately, so whatever drives it comes
straight back. headless does that in a loop with no frame pacing at all, so a
paused emulator sat at 100% of a core: measured 6.02 CPU-seconds over 6 wall
seconds parked at startBreak. A debugger session is stopped most of the time, so
this also dominated any profile taken of one - showing up as synchronization
overhead around Core_RunOnCPUThread, which was just the hottest thing inside the
spin rather than a problem with the queue.

The CPU thread now blocks on a condition variable in that case. Anything that
gives it something to do wakes it - Core_RunOnCPUThread() on push (with the
queue mutex held, so it can't sleep on a task already queued),
Core_RequestCPUStep(), and Core_Resume() - so the 2ms timeout is only a backstop
for state changed without a wake, never how work

UI: Tab and Shift+Tab move focus through the view hierarchy

Unlike the directional moves, this doesn't look at where anything ended up on
screen - it walks the hierarchy in the order views were added, flattening nested
groups in place. That's what makes it predictable in the layouts where "what's
to the right of this" has no good answer.

moves apply, so the two agree on what's reachable. Hidden subtrees are skipped
whole, which is what keeps a TabHolder's inactive tabs - V_GONE rather than
removed - out of the order without any special casing. Containers are gated on
visibility only, not enabled, matching Key/Touch/Axis: disabling a container
doesn't stop its children being interactive anywhere else either.

Interpreter: honor the guest's FPU rounding mode and flush-to-zero

Every JIT backend puts the host FPU into the mode fcr31 asks for (bits 0-1 and
24) before running emulated code, and takes it back out before calling any host
code. The plain interpreter did none of that, so all its float math rounded to
nearest with denormals intact no matter what the game had set - cpu/fpu/fpu
fails under -i and passes under the JIT on exactly this.

Move the helpers the IR interpreter already had for this out of IRInterpreter
and into MIPS.cpp as ApplyHostRoundingMode/RestoreHostRoundingMode, and use them
around the interpreter's run loop and single step, restoring around syscalls and
replacement functions, which are host code. ctc1 re-applies immediately, since
the interpreter has no block boundary to defer it to.

round.w.s changes with it: it was floorf(x + 0.5f), which is half-away-from-zero
rather than the half-to-even every JIT produces, and the add would now pick up
the guest's rounding mode
